Upon completion they will have further developed a specialisation in the areas of concept development, producing, directing, art direction, cinematography and editing.
learning_outcomes: Develop a coherent concept through ideation, mood board and storyboard, according to standard industry practice
Create a music video treatment that addresses and satisfies the requirements of a client brief
Produce, direct, shoot and edit a music video following collaborative production approaches through head of department roles and responsibilities
Apply legal and safe industry filmmaking techniques and processes during a production
Evaluate the production process as a team and critically reflect on individual roles and responsibilities

title: Advocacy
syllabus_overview: This unit develops students’ understanding and practical skills in trial and appellate advocacy. It examines courtroom procedure, case preparation, and strategic decision-making in civil and criminal contexts. Emphasis is placed on constructing and presenting persuasive legal arguments for legal proceedings in courts and tribunals, both written and oral, supported by sound legal reasoning and ethical practice. Through simulations and applied exercises, students will learn to analyse evidence, anticipate opposing arguments, and refine their professional communication techniques essential for effective advocacy in legal practice
learning_outcomes: apply legal research methods to identify, interpret, and integrate relevant authorities in the development of persuasive arguments
demonstrate effective oral and written communication skills by presenting structured, coherent, and ethically sound advocacy submissions within simulated litigation contexts
collaborate within a team to plan and evaluate litigation strategies that address procedural, evidentiary, and tactical considerations
critically evaluate the case theories, oral advocacy, and responses of others within simulated litigation contexts

title: Methods for Design Research
syllabus_overview: This unit equips students with advanced knowledge and skills in qualitative and creative research. It fosters the capacity to critically design and conduct research that addresses complex and evolving design challenges. Students engage with research design, qualitative data collection and analysis, and the development of robust, context-sensitive arguments. Emphasis is placed on generating original insights, applying research to ethical, inclusive and socially responsive design outcomes, and communicating findings effectively. Through rigorous engagement with research ethics and methodological principles, students develop the scholarly capabilities and intellectual integrity required for advanced design practice or future doctoral study.
learning_outcomes: Construct and refine a clear, original and researchable question that critically addresses a defined design objective or challenge
Evaluate and synthesise diverse and relevant scholarly and professional sources to construct a compelling rationale for the proposed research question
Design and justify a methodologically rigorous research framework, drawing on and adapting qualitative, creative, or user-centred approaches as appropriate to the research aims
Interrogate and interpret qualitative data through advanced analytical reasoning, identifying patterns, contradictions and insights that contribute meaningfully to design knowledge and practice
Critically apply and reflect on ethical research principles and protocols, demonstrating integrity, cultural sensitivity and accountability in all aspects of the research process

Synthesise research findings into a strategically informed and well-argued design proposal that clearly articulates implications for design direction and demonstrates scholarly and professional communication

title: Artificial Intelligence Transformation of Health
syllabus_overview: This unit develops students understanding for how artificial intelligence has already, or potentially can, transform health and health related outcomes in humans.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate the application of artificial intelligence in healthcare, including its use in diagnosis, prognosis, treatment, drug approval, patient care and hospital optimisation.
Evaluate the benefits, challenges, and limitations in using artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies in healthcare.
Examine new opportunities where AI-powered solutions can transform healthcare by improving traditional healthcare frameworks to address unmet needs.
Analyse and reflect on how artificial intelligence affects current and future healthcare roles.

Apply suitable artificial intelligence decision frameworks, regulatory and ethical considerations, and risk management strategies in the implementation of artificial intelligence in healthcare settings.

title: Sensation, Perception, and Attention
syllabus_overview: This unit provides an introduction to the neurobiological processes involved in perceiving and interpreting sensory information. The relationship between neural activity, perception, attention, and conscious awareness are explored. Students will engage with theoretical and empirical work to develop their understanding of the nature of consciousness.
learning_outcomes: Describe visual and auditory systems
Explain the different neurobiological mechanisms involved in sensation and perception
Contrast different attentional processes and their methods of measurement
Conduct sensory and/or perceptual and/or attentional tests with human participants
Compare, contrast, and synthesise critical arguments associated with key research in the cognitive neuroscience of sensation, perception and attention

title: Methods of Cognitive Neuroscience
syllabus_overview: This unit provides an introduction to techniques used to record neurobiological correlates of cognitive function. Students will learn how these methods relate to brain structure and function and how to interpret neuroimaging data. The unit emphasises critical thinking and evaluation of research.
learning_outcomes: Describe mechanisms of different neuroimaging techniques
Identify which neuroimaging techniques are appropriate for various neurobiological and cognitive assessments
Evaluate key strengths and limitations of various neuroimaging techniques for research and clinical applications
Critically engage with research and health-related neuroimaging literature
Design an experimental protocol involving both behavioural and neuroimaging approaches to investigate a research question in cognitive neuroscience

title: Hunger, Sex, and Sleep
syllabus_overview: This unit provides students with instruction in the neural substrates governing essential behaviours and reinforcement learning. Focusing on hunger, sex, and sleep, this unit builds on students' knowledge of brain structure and function and of cognitive processes to examine the interaction between fundamental drives and reinforcement learning to produce behaviours.
learning_outcomes: Describe the neural mechanisms underlying appetitive behaviours like sleep, sex, eating, and reinforcement learning
Explain how cognitive processes such as attention, decision-making, and memory influence and shape appetitive behaviours
Explain the role of neurotransmitters and hormones on motivations and needs, and in modulating appetitive behaviours
Critically evaluate research on models and methods used to understand disorders related to appetitive behaviours.
Compare different evidence-based interventions for the management of disorders related to appetitive behaviours and evaluate the ethical implications of these interventions

title: Technology Commercialisation
syllabus_overview: Groundbreaking research becomes the future of technology through the process of commercialisation. This unit will show students how to bridge the gap between an academic discovery and a business venture. They will have hands-on experience with real-world tools and techniques. They will learn to forecast emerging trends and protect their ideas by understanding intellectual property, patents, and tech policy. Being able to turn research results into tangible tech solutions will give students the tools they need to build a better world.
learning_outcomes: Identify emerging technologies and different innovation opportunities and trends for commercialising research
Use appropriate frameworks, tools including AI, and techniques to manage the research, technology development and innovation processes
Analyse a range of factors to make judgements about the commercial utilisation of research-based results and technology innovation outcomes
Work collaboratively to explore and interpret the challenges and societal impact of technology development and innovation
Exercise the intellectual independence to be critical and reflective learners

title: Introduction to Research Thinking for Health and Science
syllabus_overview: This unit introduces students to foundational principles of research in the fields of health and science. Students will learn about the key components of scientific inquiry such as formulating a research question and research aims, different research methods, and the philosophical paradigms that underpin different research methods. Students will also learn about the role of ethics in ensuring research integrity and safety of human participants. Students will demonstrate their ability to seek peer-reviewed literature and communicate findings from the scientific literature in different forms.
learning_outcomes: Identify and discuss the core elements of a research study in a health or science field including research aims, hypotheses, methods, results, discussion and conclusion.
Perform a review of relevant research, including searching for peer review literature using databases and selecting appropriate journal articles relevant to a health or science topic.
Describe and discuss the differences between quantitative, qualitative and mixed methods research designs in the context of health and science research.
Explain what ethical issues may arise in a human research study and strategies to mitigate ethical research issues.

title: Mathematics for Computing
syllabus_overview: This unit aims to introduce students to the fundamental mathematical concepts that underpin computer science, data analysis, AI and cybersecurity. It equips students with essential mathematical techniques in discrete mathematics, statistics, probability, and linear algebra. Students will develop analytical and problem-solving skills to model, interpret, and reason about data and systems, laying a strong foundation for further study and professional practice in digital and intelligent technologies.
learning_outcomes: Convert between binary, hexadecimal and ASCII representations of data.
Apply Boolean algebra to solve logic problems.
Use probability theories to model uncertainty and support decision-making in intelligent systems.
Calculate statistical measures and interpret data using statistical software.
Describe relationships between variables using correlation, regression, and techniques of statistical inference, using key terms appropriately.
Apply concepts in vectors and matrices to problems in data science and cyber security contexts.
Interpret and solve mathematical problems by selecting appropriate techniques and tools and communicate solutions effectively.

title: Engineering Technology with Indigenous Context
syllabus_overview: This unit aims to introduce students to the fundamental theories of electrical power systems design, electrical machines, and generation principles through completion of an engineering design project within an Indigenous cultural context. By focusing on projects related to powering Indigenous communities with innovative green energy solutions, students gain firsthand experience in applying technology to address real-world, place-based challenges. Engaging with Indigenous knowledge systems, standpoints, and culture, students learn how to collaborate effectively with communities as key stakeholders, ensuring that technological solutions are responsive to local needs and respectful of cultural values. This approach equips students with essential skills in community engagement, stakeholder communication, and adaptive problem-solving, all of which are vital for implementing technology in diverse social and environmental settings. Students will work collaboratively in teams, with a staff member acting as a facilitator throughout the project.
learning_outcomes: Explain key Electrical Engineering quantities and apply them to analyse common everyday problems
Apply Ohm’s Law, Kirchoff’s Laws and relevant theories to evaluating operation of basic AC and DC circuits
Discuss operational principles of basic electrical machines through theories of electromagnetism and describe their roles in modern power systems
Explain operations of digital circuits and logic and discuss their applications to the modern systems

Apply relevant engineering knowledge of emerging technologies to a project within an Indigenous context, incorporating appropriate frameworks, protocols, and location-specific practices to ensure respectful engagement with stakeholders
Function as an effective team member using project management tools and demonstrating professionalism and ethical behaviour

title: Problem Solving with ICT
syllabus_overview: This unit challenges students to explore different approaches to analysing and solving problems in an organisation framework. Students will develop the ability to apply analysis techniques to unfamiliar problems and present their investigation through the use of a wide range of innovative Information Communication Technologies [ICT], including prototyping, cloud-based tools, report writing and presentations. In addition, students are encouraged to reflect upon the learning taking place throughout the unit.
learning_outcomes: Identify and define problems in an organisational context
Select and apply various ICT tools and techniques to solve organisational problems
Build a solution to address an organisation problem
Evaluate the effectiveness and viability of an ICT solution from an organisational value perspective
Demonstrate working effectively in a team environment

title: Enterprise Network Server Administration
syllabus_overview: In this unit, students establish the skills and understanding required to design and configure a Windows Server based enterprise network. Student will build the skills required to design, configure and manage a single domain network.
learning_outcomes: Plan and troubleshoot a secure network access strategy
Plan and Configure advanced IP address management using DHCP and DNS
Troubleshoot network access
Plan Windows Server deployment and migration strategies
Appraise Server role requirements
Manage Server and Data Security
Design a policy strategy within an Active Directory infrastructure

title: Airline Crew Planning and Resourcing
syllabus_overview: The aim of this unit is to provide students with in-depth understanding of crew resource management and its practical applications. The unit covers key aspects of crew contracts and agreements, as well as the impacts of good and poor rostering on crew fatigue and operational risks. The unit is designed to equip students with broader workforce planning considerations, including scheduling strategies and disruption management, to ensure safe and efficient airline operations.
learning_outcomes: Explain the key principles of airline crewing philosophy, objectives, and operational efficiencies, along with the challenges associated with crew management
Integrate regulatory and operational requirements into crew planning and rostering practices
Discern key elements of crew contracts and agreements and apply this knowledge in crew roster creation
Recognise and assess human-related issues relating to short and long-haul duty periods, fatigue, rest, and acclimatisation

Identify and apply short and long-term manpower planning strategies to match crew supply with demand, and address issues such as duty limits, accommodation, and transportation, particularly during disruptions
Explain normal crew procedures and practices occurring on a daily basis for various types of operations
Construct a set of realistic crew rosters using appropriate software, taking legal and other frameworks into account

title: Principles of Financial Planning
syllabus_overview: This unit aims to provide an overview of the financial planning industry. Students will learn about the background and purpose of financial planning legislations and the relevant code of conducts. They will also learn the financial advice process and the steps involved in construction and communication of a Statement of Advice, considering clientsâ€™ objectives and needs. This unit introduces the management of a financial planning practice. Students will also be introduced to relevant technologies, client engagement process and ethical principles in Financial Planning.
learning_outcomes: Identify scope of financial advice and demonstrate knowledge of financial advice processes and technologies
Exhibit an understanding of legislation and codes of conduct in the financial planning industry
Develop a Statement of Advice for clients while considering the relevant ethical principles and professional conduct requirements
Demonstrate professional communication skills, in order to effectively articulate an idea and convince others of its merit
Work collaboratively and effectively in teams

title: Advanced Electronics Design
syllabus_overview: This unit of study aims to introduce students to electronics design in micro and nano electronic systems. Students will learn, to design, analyse, implement and test analog, digital and mixed signal circuits. Students will learn to use of advanced industry standard Electronic Design Automation Tools for schematic entry, simulation, layout and verification. Students will understand tradeoffs between low power, speed of operation, chip area and noise. At the end of the unit students will be able to apply design principles to build verify different Integrated Circuit subsystems.
learning_outcomes: Apply CMOS technology principles to transistor-level circuit design
Design and implement analogue building blocks such as amplifiers, bias circuits, current mirrors.
Design and verify digital logic using standard cells and custom layouts.
Identify, analyse and address layout-related issues (e.g. parasitics, latch-up, mismatch).
Design and Implement a complete mixed-signal IC subsystem using modern design flows.

title: Engineering Master Thesis
syllabus_overview: To provide students with the opportunity to conduct research into theory and techniques learnt in the course, and apply it in solving relevant industry based or applied research problems in the area of specialisation.
learning_outcomes: Plan and scope a complete research / design project
Formulate a design solution based on thorough literature research by applying, executing and synthesising knowledge
Research and develop alternative solutions to the design problem and appraise and justify the chosen solution in terms of its creativity and level of difficulty
Reflect on engineering design and research issues
Apply and formulate problem-solving techniques to evaluate, appraise and justify alternative design solutions
Generate a high quality master's degree minor thesis that incorporates literature review, requirements analysis, project/research plan, design, and implementation

title: Wireless Communication Techniques
syllabus_overview: This unit is designed to allow students to gain a broad understanding of the signal processing and modulation concepts and methods that underpin analogue and digital transmission for wireless communications.
learning_outcomes: Explain common terminology, concepts, equipment and techniques of signal processing for communications (K2, S1)
Explain, justify, analyse and critically evaluate common signal processing concepts and methods (A2, K3)
Analyse signals and determine their spectra (K2, S1, S2)
Analyse the performance of various modulation methods for analogue transmission (A2, S1, S2)
Analyse the performance of various modulation methods for digital transmission (A2, S1, S2)
Evaluate the effect of noise on signal reception (K2, S1)
Assemble signal processing modules to implement communications systems (K3, K6, S2)

title: Ideas, Opportunities and Ventures
syllabus_overview: The entrepreneurial process is key to both starting a business and innovating within an existing organisation. This unit will teach students how to use the entrepreneurial process to generate ideas, find the best opportunities, and build successful business ventures. They will learn to understand people’s needs, discover the world of megatrends and competitive forces, and identify industry drivers. They will use frameworks, tools and techniques to evaluate ideas and learn to analyse entrepreneurial opportunities. Students will leave equipped with strategies to overcome challenges and the tools to grow their ideas.
learning_outcomes: Identify different sources of ideas and generate business ideas
Use appropriate frameworks, tools and techniques to evaluate ideas and identify opportunities
Analyse a range of factors to make judgements about entrepreneurial opportunities
Work collaboratively to explore and interpret the challenges of entrepreneurial ventures
Exercise the intellectual independence to be critical and reflective learners

title: Understanding Sexually Violent and Harassing Behaviours
syllabus_overview: The formulation of complex behaviour is a process where factors that underpin behaviours are examined to determine appropriate treatment targets and interventions. Forensic behavioural formulation is specifically interested in understanding what drives problematic behaviours such as violence, sexual violence, threats, fire setting and stalking. By understanding what is influencing a behaviour we can then find ways to support stopping the behaviour.
learning_outcomes: Formulate the role of distal, proximal, individual and contextual factors for a range of sexually violent problem behaviours

Critique the theoretical and empirical research and contributory role of different factors into different types of problem behaviours, considering their relevance and expression across marginalised populations, including Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples
Assess the contributory role of different risk factors across different types of problem behaviours, based on an understanding of relevant empirical research

Apply the problem behaviour framework to individual cases to guide the development of appropriate treatment and management plans for people who have engaged in sexual offending, stalking, and abnormal complaining

title: Indigenous Representations
syllabus_overview: Building on the knowledge gained in pre-requisite units, this unit further develops studentsâ€™ knowledge of Indigenous Australian issues and further emphasise the diversity of Indigenous Australia and its people. It provides a solid understanding of the pervasive power of colonial representations and the ways in which these have functioned during the â€˜contact periodâ€™ (1770-present) to shape non-Indigenous understandings of Australiaâ€™s Indigenous peoples. The unit also investigates the impact that representational constructs have had in shaping the lives Indigenous Australians, and the role of all citizens in this investigation.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate an understanding of the way that Australia has historically created knowledge about Indigenous Australians, and the historical dissemination of this knowledge

Show a basic understanding of the power of language in the construction of representational racial and cultural identity and the implications of these images, stories, stereotypes and tropes on the life choices of Indigenous Australians
Understand and identify the extant, pervasive effects of colonialism on contemporary Australian society
Confidently practise and further encourage broader thinking in issues of inter-cultural relationships in contemporary Australia

Research a number of topics relating to Indigenous Australians and present a balanced, supported argument that contributes to informed discussions of Indigenous issues in Australia and inter-cultural discussions in general

title: Preliminary Mathematics
syllabus_overview: This unit of study aims to provide students with the preliminary mathematical knowledge and skills to support their concurrent and subsequent studies, providing a thorough grounding in mathematics and laying a foundation for further studies.
learning_outcomes: Describe the locus graphically in Cartesian co-ordinates and polar co-ordinates. Represent the equation of the locus in Cartesian form and polar form and identify the graph represented
Define circular functions, identify the graphs of trigonometric functions, and solve trigonometric equations

Use the index laws and logarithm laws to manipulate exponential and logarithmic expressions and, solve the exponential equation using the logarithmic method. Determine empirical rule for data related by exponential law. Apply exponential and logarithm functions in practical problems

Explain the meaning of limit notation and evaluate the derivative of a function using the concept of limit. Apply the rules of differentiation to evaluate the derivatives of polynomial, trigonometric, inverse trigonometric, exponential, and logarithmic functions
Apply differentiation to find maxima/minima and solve problems in curve sketching
Evaluate the indefinite and definite integrals by techniques of integration and interpret the physical significance of definite integral. Apply definite integration to evaluate the bounded area
Introduction to 2D Vectors

title: Typography
syllabus_overview: This unit introduces students to and facilitates a fundamental understanding of, typographic forms, terminology, typesetting systems and conventions, grid structure and hierarchy using a variety of technologies. The unit aims to develop a critical awareness of the visual relationships between content and meaning through the exploration, application of typographic form with layout and design principles.
learning_outcomes: Describe aspects of typographic history, development and terminology
Apply typographic expression and visual experimentation appropriately to the context in which it is used
Apply typographic classification and conventions to achieve effective sequential or structured communication for a variety of contexts
Report on the research and design development in typographic projects to achieve communication objectives
Construct complex narrative and interrelated designs and layouts with type and image
Appraise and reflect on the effectiveness of the design and development of typographic outcomes in relation to communication objectives

title: Interior Architecture Communication
syllabus_overview: This unit aims to introduce students to visual communication through sketching, photography, 2D and 3D drawing using art and architectural precedents. It provides students with basic skills of orthographic (hardline), axonometric and perspective drawing. The unit also provides students with understanding of spaces and forms via conceptual model making and drawing. The unit will focus on studio skills building within a series of small tasks and a final skill-consolidation project.
learning_outcomes: Analyse and explain design drawing and drawing techniques specific to Architecture (A2, A4)
Consider and articulate experiential space as a constructed interior environment (A6, S3)
Visually convey space, planning and human environments using industry-relevant methods (K3, K5, S3)
Apply basic model-making techniques (conceptual model) to a formal presentation project (A2, K2)
Apply basic drawing techniques (Architectural orthographic and perspective drawings) to a formal presentation project (A2, A5)
Negotiate between 2D and 3D representation (A2, K2)
Explore and articulate the effect of light and materials through observation, hand model making, rendering and photographic documentation (A2, A6, K1)

title: Introductory Design Studio
syllabus_overview: The unit introduces students to fundamental approaches to generating form and to the principles which inform design decisions. Students work across two-dimensional and three-dimensional representation methods, using a range of materials and fabrication techniques at different scales as they generate concepts and communicate outcomes. Through project-based, experiential learning in tandem with theoretical presentation of fundamental techniques and principles, students will gain the ability to analyse and articulate design principles, materials and relationships through their work. As the unit introduces students to workshop techniques, an induction to workshop occupational health and safety protocols is a required component of the unit.
learning_outcomes: Identify the relationship between form, material and technology in the context of human scale (S2, S3)
Apply manual and digital fabrication techniques to design and make artefacts in response to a brief
Create new designs with consideration of material use and constructibility
Utilise compositional principles and material processes to develop new artefacts
Visually communicate design projects
Apply Occupational Health and Safety requirements of safe workshop practices to design projects (A5, A6, K6, S1)

title: Learning Through Professional Practicum
syllabus_overview: This unit aims to have students fulfil the 200-hours of practicum requirement and will contain practicum elements in the form of
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate professional teaching capability through satisfactory completion of supervised practicum activities in a VET context, aligned with regulatory standards and institutional expectations
Critically reflect on key theoretical concepts in relation to professional practice and your own teaching and learning philosophy to debate strengths, challenges, and opportunities

Apply pedagogical and assessment principles in authentic VET settings, integrating theory with practice to support learner engagement and competency development, including direct instruction, observation, and participation in organisational and learner-focused activities
Document and evaluate practicum activities as evidence of professional development, and opportunities for growth in vocational teaching and assessment practice

title: Assessing Learning and Competency in Vocational Education
syllabus_overview: This unit equips VET educators (established and emergining) with a deep understanding of assessment principles and practices specific to vocational education. It explores the design and implementation of competency-based assessments aligned with training packages and workplace learning. Through critical reflection and practical application, educators will develop the skills to create inclusive, valid, and reliable assessments that meet regulatory and industry standards. The unit fosters professional growth and supports educators in evidencing their capability to assess student learning and contribute to quality assurance in VET.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate the principles and regulatory requirements underpinning assessment in the VET sector.
Design and develop competency-based formative and summative assessments aligned with training packages.
Apply inclusive and diverse feedback methods to support learner development in vocational contexts.
Evaluate and improve assessment practices through reflective and evidence-based approaches.

title: Moving Image Arts
syllabus_overview: This unit develops an understanding of moving image arts through experimental film and screen production for and beyond the cinema screen. Through critical engagement with existing moving image arts projects, students will gain creative skill sets and competencies in experimental approaches for the Screen Industry. Students will produce audio-visual experiences and investigate the potential of emerging media for creative innovation in exhibition contexts and on non-tradition screens (such a public screens and/or Cinematic VR).
learning_outcomes: Evaluate the role of experimental filmmaking in the contemporary sector of the Film and Television industries
Identify a range of screen work with contemporary and historical approaches within experimental film and video, mobile and smartphone filmmaking and emerging media in moving image arts
Evaluate different methods of moving image production in delivering Film and Television products for non-traditional screens
Produce experimental screen outcomes for the cinema screen, exhibition experiences and non-traditional screens that apply coherent production and post-production processes
Explore experimentation processes relevant for film and television industry

title: Marketing Automation
syllabus_overview: This unit aims to develop students’ understanding and competency in using marketing automation as a strategic organisational lever for managing customer relationships. Students will learn how organisations design, orchestrate, and optimise automated customer journeys by integrating customer data, customer relationship management (CRM) systems, analytics, artificial intelligence, and digital channels. The unit emphasises applied, ethical, and data‑driven decision‑making to deliver personalised customer experiences at scale.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate the role of marketing automation as a strategic capability, and its relevance to professional development.
Design and justify automated customer journeys that integrate customer data, segmentation, triggers, and multi‑channel touchpoints to deliver personalised experiences at scale.
Analyse and optimise marketing automation programs using appropriate lifecycle metrics, experimentation, and performance evaluation techniques.
Critically assess ethical, privacy, and governance considerations associated with the use of customer data, personalisation, and automated decision‑making in marketing contexts.
Demonstrate certifications and competence in using industry best-practice marketing automation technology platforms.

title: Search Marketing
syllabus_overview: This unit aims to develop students’ conceptual understanding and competency in search engine marketing as a core component of digital marketing strategy. Students will examine how search engines function and how organisations use search engine optimisation (SEO) and paid search (Search Engine Marketing / Pay-Per-Click Advertising) to attract, acquire, and convert customers. The unit emphasises keyword strategy, search intent, content optimisation, paid search campaign design, and performance measurement. Through applied activities and real‑world scenarios, students will design, implement, and optimise search marketing initiatives using data‑driven insights, while considering ethical, privacy, and platform governance issues in contemporary search marketing practice.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate the role of search marketing as a strategic capability, and its relevance to professional development
Design an integrated search engine marketing strategy, incorporating SEO and SEM, to support organisational goals, while considering ethical and legal issues
Evaluate search intent, behaviour, and interaction using keyword research, competitive analysis, and search analytics tools
Implement and optimise search marketing campaigns by interpreting performance data and recommending evidence‑based improvements
Demonstrate certifications and competence in using industry best-practice search marketing technology platforms

title: Project Planning and Delivery
syllabus_overview: This unit aims to develop students’ capability to plan, coordinate, and monitor projects in organisational contexts using structured project management approaches, tools, and performance measures. Students will learn how to scope projects, develop schedules and resource plans, manage risks, and evaluate project performance against organisational objectives. The unit emphasises disciplined project delivery, evidence-based decision-making, and the practical use of project management software in contemporary workplace settings
learning_outcomes: Determine the role of project planning and delivery as a professional capability within organisational contexts
Evaluate and apply appropriate project planning approaches to suit diverse organisational contexts, project requirements, and support effective project delivery
Work effectively within a team to develop project artefacts, including scope documents, schedules, resource plans, and cost baselines, using appropriate tools and industry standard software
Apply project monitoring and performance measures to evaluate progress, analyse project risks, constraints, dependencies, and recommend mitigation and control strategies
Demonstrate certifications and competence in industry best-practice project planning and delivery

title: Experimental Game Design
syllabus_overview: This unit focuses upon experimentation and innovation with fundamental concepts of game design and play across multiple media. Research and presentation methods, group work and communication, planning and production are essential to the design process. This unit builds on knowledge from other units to explore the platform of experimental game design using the campus as a playground, with links to other forms of media including film, theatre, television, and the digital arts. In this unit, game design principles are expanded upon, and experimented with, through the development, promotion and play of game projects.
learning_outcomes: Critically reflect on the relationship between games and culture in experimental game design
Synthesise broad discipline knowledge and theory to develop a working knowledge within an area of specialisation
Analyse aspects of narrative, mechanics, aesthetics and technology involved in experimental game designs and platforms, and communicate these a range of audiences
Apply knowledge and skills with responsibility and accountability for their own learning and practice
Function and communicate effectively as an individual and in project teams, whether as manager, leader or team member

title: Essential Skills for Career Success
syllabus_overview: This unit aims to equip students with the reflective, professional, and career development capabilities required to navigate contemporary business environments and plan for long-term career success. Students will develop self-awareness, ethical judgement, adaptability, and professional identity, while building the capacity to evaluate their strengths, articulate their value, and plan their future development. Through reflective practice, industry engagement, and career-oriented learning activities, the unit prepares students to manage their professional growth, build a credible professional presence, and navigate transitions from university to work.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate personal strengths, values, and development needs to support self-awareness and ongoing professional growth
Apply strategies to manage wellbeing, resilience, and psychological safety in academic and early career contexts
Develop and articulate a professional identity informed by reflection on personal strengths, capabilities, and career aspirations
Curate and present a professional portfolio that demonstrates readiness for contemporary business and technology-enabled workplaces
Develop a career development plan informed by reflection, industry insight, and future workforce expectations

title: Accounting, Society and Sustainability
syllabus_overview: This unit aims to provide students with a comprehensive understanding of the theoretical frameworks that underpin the discipline of accounting. Students will critically explore and apply accounting theories to explain accounting decisions and organisational outcomes in contemporary financial and non-financial reporting contexts. The unit places a strong emphasis on addressing real-world accounting and societal challenges, with a particular focus on sustainability and climate-related financial disclosures.
learning_outcomes: Critically evaluate the theoretical frameworks, regulatory approaches, and political forces that influence contemporary accounting practices
Apply accounting theories to analyse complex organisational scenarios and justify accounting decisions, accounting for ethical, societal, governance and Indigenous considerations
Analyse and apply various sustainability reporting frameworks and related concepts, focusing on the contemporary application of climate risk reporting in the Australian context
Exercise critical thinking and professional judgment to identify and assess accounting challenges, including issues related to the relevance, usefulness, and societal impact of accounting information

Conduct research, analyse, and discuss complex contemporary financial and non-financial reporting issues, develop well-reasoned and coherent arguments, and draw well-considered conclusions on those issues

title: Cost Planning Project
syllabus_overview: This is a WIL SPINE unit which aims to develop students’ capability to strategically plan and manage construction costs across the project lifecycle by applying cost planning principles, estimating techniques, and design economics. Students will work with relevant industry partner to prepare, analyse, communicate, and optimise cost plans that support project feasibility, value engineering, and informed decision‑making for building and infrastructure projects. Students will develop and apply skills in using computer tools like CostX, professional written communication, project planning, stakeholder engagement and decision making in construction projects.
learning_outcomes: Explain the principles, processes, and strategic role of construction cost planning in managing project feasibility and financial performance across the project lifecycle.
Prepare cost plans for building and infrastructure projects using appropriate estimating techniques and cost data
Integrate design economics principles to evaluate cost implications of design decisions, materials, procurement strategies and construction methods to support value engineering and cost optimisation.
Use digital tools and workflows to develop, communicate, and report construction cost plans

title: Application of Advanced Construction Technologies
syllabus_overview: This unit aims to develop students’ understanding of construction procurement and the application of digital technologies in project delivery. Students will evaluate and recommend appropriate procurement routes, manage scope and change digitally, and apply in‑situ and remote monitoring technologies to improve construction quality, productivity, and safety across diverse project contexts.
learning_outcomes: Explain various procurement methods used in a construction project.
Evaluate and advise on the appropriateness of various procurement routes/methods.
Employ digital technologies for scope and change management in construction project delivery
Apply digital technologies for in-situ and remote monitoring of construction site operations to manage quality, productivity and safety

title: Design Capstone Project 2
syllabus_overview: This capstone unit aims to synthesise and integrate students’ knowledge of design theory, disciplinary principles, and creative processes into a professionally oriented design project. Through engagement with a structured creative brief, students will consolidate their capabilities in applied design, critical thinking, problem solving, communication, intellectual autonomy, and collaborative practice. The unit fosters exploration of emerging opportunities across diverse design contexts while reinforcing core design competencies and professional skills essential for entry into contemporary design practice.
learning_outcomes: Apply creative problem solving, critical thinking and research skills to answer a complex design brief.
Synthesise appropriate design methods, processes, techniques, technologies and tools to create a design outcome to a professional standard.
Demonstrate professional competencies in communication, collaboration and time management.
Communicate the design process and outcomes through concise, coherent and well-structured documentation and presentations.

Critically reflect on individual design strengths, professional skills and attributes, and formative feedback to deliver a design project that exhibits innovative thinking and a high standard of creative practice.

title: Social Media Marketing
syllabus_overview: This unit aims to develop students’ strategic and practical capabilities in social media marketing as a core component of contemporary digital marketing strategy. Students will examine how organisations use social media platforms to build brand awareness, presence, engage audiences, and support customer acquisition and retention. The unit focuses on social media strategy development, content creation, platform selection, influencer and community management, advertising, and performance measurement using analytics. Students will design, implement, and evaluate social media marketing campaigns while considering ethical, legal, and governance issues that shape responsible social media practice
learning_outcomes: Determine the role of social media as a strategic capability, and its relevance to professional development
Design and implement a social media marketing strategy that meets business objectives and engages a brand's target audience, while considering ethical and legal constraints
Create and manage social media content that drives acquisition, engagement, conversion, and other measurable marketing outcomes
Analyse social media performance data to evaluate effectiveness and make evidence‑based optimisation recommendations
Demonstrate certifications and competence in using industry best-practice social media marketing technology platforms

title: AI Ad Lab
syllabus_overview: AI Ad Lab is a hands-on creative production unit for Year 2 advertising students focused on practical use of generative AI tools. Students develop skills to concept, produce and evaluate advertising creative across image, video and audio formats using industry-standard platforms. The unit progresses from AI tool literacy to independent creative production, culminating in a multi-format campaign. Students work with AI systems for creative production, ideation and productivity, and AI-enabled design and post-production, supported by additional tools for display and video editing. Alongside technical capability, the unit builds critical thinking around authorship, quality, brand voice and ethical use of AI, preparing students for advanced study and professional practice in an AI-shaped industry.
learning_outcomes: Apply prompt engineering and creative direction techniques to develop brand-consistent AI-generated advertising content.
Develop and produce a multi-format advertising campaign using AI creative platforms across image, video and audio formats
Evaluate AI-generated creative work against strategic advertising objectives, brand guidelines and industry quality standards
Critically reflect on the ethical, creative and professional implications of AI-assisted advertising production

title: Screen Audiences
syllabus_overview: This unit uncovers the vital role of audiences in screen culture. It introduces students to how viewers, fans, and gamers have been theorised by scholars and understood by the creative industries. Students explore audiences for film, TV shows, games, and broader screen culture to understand global consumption practices, cross-generational trends, and overlooked screen communities. Students develop an understanding of how audience practices are shaped by technology, media policy, and industry regulation. Crucially, this unit will instruct students in key audience research methods, equipping them with skills that are in demand across a range of screen culture roles.
learning_outcomes: Critically examine scholarly and industry approaches to identifying and researching screen audiences
Analyse audiences across platforms, generations, and global contexts
Evaluate how audience behaviours are shaped by technology, media policy, and industry regulation
Apply the best methods for audience research and communicate insights to industry and community stakeholders

title: Multiplatform Media Production and Practice
syllabus_overview: This unit aims to equip students with the skills to report, write, record, shoot, and deliver news and information across a range of online and multiplatform media. Students will develop a critical understanding of multiplatform production and practice, while gaining proficiency in writing and publishing for online and multiplatform environments.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse and evaluate the networked resources used in contemporary multiplatform practice and production
Create integrated media content for online publications using multiplatform tools and techniques
Research and critically evaluate ways to create written, image and audio storytelling across industry-adopted publishing platforms and technologies
Synthesise independent research and knowledge of practical tools, methods, legal and ethical standards to conceptualise and evaluate news media for a range of platforms

title: Social Science, Law and Crime
syllabus_overview: This unit aims to develop awareness of the major disciplines in the social sciences (criminological, psychological, sociological), and how these perspectives influence responses to crime in society. Students will examine perspective of various social sciences and consider the strengths and challenges these perspectives bring in terms of how we understand crime and our approaches to preventing criminal behaviour across policy, system, service, and individual levels. The unit will help students develop critical thinking about different ways of thinking about crime and be able to identify the impact of disciplinary perspectives on the effectiveness and outcome of societal responses to crime.
learning_outcomes: Identify key concepts from criminological, psychological, sociological, and legal perspectives on crime.
Describe the ways each discipline contributes to understanding crime and criminal behaviour.
Compare the strengths and limitations of different disciplinary approaches to crime and its prevention.
Analyse the challenges in integrating multiple perspectives when addressing crime at various levels (policy, service, individual).
Evaluate arguments regarding the causes and prevention of crime from different disciplinary viewpoints.
Critically assess how multiple perspectives can inform more effective crime prevention strategies and criminal justice practices.

title: Social Media Communication
syllabus_overview: This unit provides students with an understanding of the intersection of Strategic Communication and Social Media. It provides students with appropriate methodologies for managing reputation in a social media environment, and a critical competency of communicating using social media.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse and discuss the role of social media within integrated communication strategies
Apply analytical and communication skills to create targeted and effective social media content
Synthesise ethical considerations and responsibilities to guide the creation of socially responsible social media communications
Identify, evaluate, and respond to the needs of diverse social media audiences through tailored communication approaches

title: Advanced Road Engineering
syllabus_overview: This unit is intended to be an elective within the Civil Engineering degree program, which will provide students with an extended knowledge in the specific discipline of road and pavement engineering. Topics include (i) the role of roads in the national economy, (ii) route selection, layout and geometric alignment, (iii) site investigation practices, (iv) design of the pavement structure, (v) road construction, and (vi) principles of road maintenance and asset management via an overall pavement management system.
learning_outcomes: Critically discuss the important micro and macroeconomic contributions of the road pavement network (A2, K5)

Evaluate the key factors affecting the structural behaviour of road pavements and compare road pavements under different operating environments through the application of fundamental elastic theories (A2, K1, K3, S1, S2)
Undertake a desk top route selection and appreciate the underpinning tenets of geometric alignment (A2, K1, K2, K3, S1, S2, S3)
Design a representative soil sampling and testing regime to determine subgrade support criteria and soil behaviour (A2, K1, K3, S1, S2, S3)
Describe the broad range of failure modes of materials and compare the wide spectrum of pavement materials to optimise road pavement performance through contemporary standards (K1, K3, K5, S1)

Undertake the empirical design of sealed granular and thick asphalt flexible pavements. Appraise and optimise the selection of road pavements through the application of example design charts (A2, K1, K2, K3, K6, S1, S2, S3)
Apply the broad principles of project management, quality systems and specifications to road construction (K1, K3, S3, S4)
Critically apply whole of life performance criteria to evaluate roads as physical infrastructure assets (K1, K3, K5, S1)

title: Introduction to Quantum Computation and Applications of Quantum Technologies
syllabus_overview: This unit aims to provide students with an accessible introduction to quantum computation and quantum technologies, focusing on a conceptual understanding. It develops intuition about qubits, quantum circuits, and probabilistic computation, and how these differ from classical computing. The unit also aims to build awareness of current and emerging quantum applications, enabling students to critically assess the capabilities, limitations, and potential impact of quantum technologies on industry, society, and the computing profession.
learning_outcomes: Discuss and communicate real‑world applications of quantum technologies and evaluate their potential impact on industry, society, and the computing profession
Describe, in plain language, the key ideas behind quantum computation and explain how they differ from classical computing concepts
Explain how quantum computation is represented using simple circuit diagrams and interpret the behaviour of small quantum circuits at a conceptual and probabilistic level
Run simple quantum programs using a high‑level quantum programming environment or simulator
Analyse which types of problems quantum computers are potentially useful for, and identify key limitations of current quantum technologies compared with classical computing

title: Web Design and Analytics
syllabus_overview: This unit aims to develop students’ capability to plan, design, build, publish, and evaluate effective web‑based experiences for contemporary marketing contexts. Students will integrate principles of visual design, brand identity, user experience, accessibility, inclusivity, and interaction design with foundational web technologies and content management systems. Through hands‑on practice and applied projects, students will create responsive, fit‑for‑purpose websites and applications, articulate design rationales, and optimise content for diverse users, devices, and bandwidth conditions. The unit also builds awareness of web analytics, discoverability, and ethical considerations underpinning modern digital marketing and communication.
learning_outcomes: Determine the role of web design and analytics as a strategic marketing capability, and its relevance to professional development
Design websites and applications that align with an organisation’s visual identity, brand style guide, and market positioning
Apply UX design principles to build websites and applications that support functionality, responsiveness, engagement, accessibility, and inclusivity, while considering legal and ethical issues
Evaluate the performance of websites and applications using web analytics, using metrics and key performance indicators that align with marketing objectives
Demonstrate certifications and competence in using industry best-practice web design and analytics technology platforms

title: Postgraduate Bureau Internship
syllabus_overview: This unit is designed to deepen students’ understanding of research-led professional design practice while cultivating advanced employability and design strategy skills. Through an internship hosted by Swinburne University, students will engage in directed, experiential learning within a work-integrated context, applying research-led knowledge, and strategic design methods to real-world tasks and projects for diverse clients. Complementary learning activities will further enhance professional capabilities, encouraging students to critically reflect on their industry experience and confidently articulate their emerging professional identity.
learning_outcomes: Independently apply research-led knowledge and design practice methods to tasks within a work integrated learning context
Effectively and collaboratively participate and contribute to a professional design practice environment
Prepare design solutions in response to industry briefs that are informed by design research, and consideration of intellectual property, ethical practice and emerging technologies
Critically reflect on one’s research-led design practice and pursue one’s professional purpose

title: Advanced Postgraduate Bureau Internship
syllabus_overview: This unit is designed to deepen and extend students’ understanding of research-led professional design practice while cultivating advanced employability, design strategy and leadership skills. Through an internship hosted by Swinburne University, students will engage in directed, experiential learning within a work-integrated context. They will apply research-led knowledge, and strategic design methods to real-world tasks and projects for diverse clients, evaluate outcomes and develop leadership capabilities. Complementary learning activities will further enhance professional attributes, encouraging students to critically reflect on their industry experience and confidently articulate their emerging professional identity.
learning_outcomes: Proactively apply research-led knowledge and design practice methods to tasks within a work integrated learning context
Manage and collaboratively participate and contribute to a professional design practice environment, including through leadership and mentoring
Formulate design solutions in response to industry briefs that are informed by considerations of intellectual property, ethical practice and emerging technologies
Critically reflect on one’s research-led design practice, plan strategies for personal development, and demonstrate development of professional purpose

title: Water Engineering
syllabus_overview: This unit of study aims to develop further understanding of sustainability as it applies to water engineering and, of the basic engineering principles and analysis techniques to design a water supply system.
learning_outcomes: Conduct scientific research using appropriate sources of data and interpret and synthesise these in terms of ongoing scientific debates (K1, K4, K5, S1, S2, S4, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7)

Discuss and debate the most effective means of dealing with current and future water shortages in an urban context with an appreciation for climate change and sustainability issues (K4, K5, K6, S2, A2, A5, A7)

Plan and design a recycled water pipeline, assess alternative design strategies in terms of economic, social and environmental factors and justify your design in terms of these factors and standard engineering principles and practices (K2, K3, K5, K6, S1, S2, S3, S4, A1, A2, A3, A4, A6, A7)
Appraise and assess the quality of your colleagues’ project work and presentation skills and reflect upon your own experiences within your project team (A4, A5, A6, A7)
Discuss and interpret your research and/or design findings with a your professional colleagues by conducting a professional presentation (K4, K5, S1, S2, S3, S4, A2, A4, A5, A7)
Demonstrate your negotiation, planning, management, research and analysis skills to form an effective part of a project team (S2, S4, A2, A5, A6, A7)

title: Strategic Communication and Storytelling
syllabus_overview: This unit aims to develop students’ capability to communicate ideas persuasively and professionally through presentations and storytelling in organisational contexts. Students will learn how to analyse audiences, structure compelling messages, design effective visual and verbal communication, and deliver persuasive presentations that communicate proposals, recommendations, and strategic ideas in workplace settings. The unit emphasises credibility, clarity, audience alignment, and persuasive impact in professional communication settings.
learning_outcomes: Determine the role of strategic communication and storytelling as a professional capability within organisational contexts
Analyse audiences, stakeholders, and communication objectives to design appropriate presentation and storytelling strategies
Work effectively within a team to create professional presentations using effective verbal, visual, and non-verbal communication techniques
Apply persuasion to structure narratives, presentations, and supporting materials that communicate value clearly and coherently to influence decision-making and support organisational objectives
Demonstrate certifications and competence in industry best-practice presentation and storytelling

title: Collaborative Problem Solving and Stakeholder Engagement
syllabus_overview: This unit aims to develop students’ capability to work collaboratively to diagnose and solve complex organisational problems while building and managing effective stakeholder relationships. Students will learn how to frame problems, analyse stakeholder needs and interests, generate and evaluate solutions, and navigate collaboration challenges in dynamic workplace settings. The unit emphasises negotiation, conflict management, communication, and ethical judgement as applied capabilities for achieving shared outcomes. Through authentic scenarios and team-based activities, students will build practical capability in managing relationships, influencing decision-making, and delivering responsible solutions in organisational and professional contexts.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate the roles of collaborative problem solving and stakeholder engagement as professional capabilities within organisational contexts.
Analyse organisational problems and stakeholder contexts to generate evidence-based solutions that balance organisational objectives, stakeholder interests, and ethical considerations.
Apply collaboration, negotiation, and conflict management strategies to work effectively with diverse stakeholders and teams in professional contexts.
Recommend stakeholder engagement approaches that build trust, alignment, and constructive working relationships in organisational settings.
Demonstrate certifications and competence in industry best-practice collaboration, problem solving, and relationship management

title: Water Engineering Design Project
syllabus_overview: This WIL Spine unit aims to further develop students’ understanding of water sustainability and environmental issues while undertaking water engineering design projects with relevant industry partners. These include applying engineering design principles and techniques as well as current industry design standards to produce water engineering projects of social, economic and environmental relevance to the industry and diverse communities.The students will respond to project briefs and consider relevant local, state, and federal regulations to achieve their project outcomes. Students will develop skills in using computer tools including AutoCAD and Excel for data and information analysis, interpretation, professional communication and presentation of their water engineering design projects. Students will apply professional skills in Teamwork, Communication, Cultural competency skills, Innovation and complex problem solving, and Sustainability.
learning_outcomes: Conduct scientific research using appropriate sources of data and interpret and synthesise these in terms of ongoing scientific debates (K1, K4, K5, S1, S2, S4, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7)

Discuss and debate the most effective means of dealing with current and future water shortages in an urban context with an appreciation for climate change and sustainability issues (K4, K5, K6, S2, A2, A5, A7)

Plan and design a recycled water pipeline system that complies with standard engineering principles and practices; takes into consideration economic, social, and environmental factors; and acknowledges indigenous cultures. (K2, K3, K5, K6, S1, S2, S3, S4, A1, A2, A3, A4, A6, A7)
Appraise and assess the quality of colleagues’ project work and presentation skills and reflect upon their own experiences within the project team (A4, A5, A6, A7)
Discuss and interpret research and/or design findings with professional colleagues by conducting a professional presentation (K4, K5, S1, S2, S3, S4, A2, A4, A5, A7)
Demonstrate negotiation, planning, management, research and analysis skills to form an effective part of a project team (S2, S4, A2, A5, A6, A7)

title: Bridge Design and Strengthening
syllabus_overview: Bridge Design and Strengthening unit aims to equip students with advanced knowledge and practical skills in the analysis, design, and strengthening of bridge structures. The course covers fundamental bridge types, structural forms, and construction methods, enabling students to select appropriate designs based on project requirements. Through structural modeling and load application, students develop the ability to analyze bridge decks and undertake preliminary designs of prestressed concrete and steel members. A key focus is on the application of strengthening solutions, including the use of fiber-reinforced polymers (FRP) for structural enhancement.
learning_outcomes: Describe the common structural forms for bridges and select an appropriate structural form for a specific bridging task (K1,K3,K4,K5,K6,S1,S2,S3)
Develop a structural analysis model for a beam and slab bridge and apply loading representative of a moving vehicle (K1,K2,K3,K4,K6,S3)
Undertake preliminary design of selected bridge members in prestressed concrete and steel materials (K1,K2,K3,K4,K5,K6,S1,S2,S3)
Understand the causes of structural deterioration and identify suitable strengthening techniques (K1, K3, S1, S2)
Design externally bonded composite strengthening schemes for structural elements for flexure shear and axial loads (K1, K3, S1, S2, S3)
Function individually to design a strengthening solution for a reinforced concrete girder considering different loading actions, constructability and structural safety. (K1, K3, S1, S2, S3)

title: Measurement and Estimation
syllabus_overview: This unit aims to develop students’ competencies in construction measurement and cost estimating for commercial and infrastructure projects. It covers interpreting drawings, applying ANZSMM, and using BIM tools to produce quantities and cost estimates across project phases.
learning_outcomes: Read and interpret construction drawings and specifications relevant to Infrastructure construction projects
Apply Australian and New Zealand Standard Method of Measurement (ANZSMM) to measure and prepare bills of quantities of commercial and infrastructure construction projects
Prepare various levels of cost estimates for different project phases using recognised estimating principles
Estimate unit rates for construction activities to support tender preparation for building and infrastructure projects
Utilise Building Information Modelling (BIM) tools for measurements and estimation

title: Digital Coordination and Communication in Construction
syllabus_overview: The aim of this unit is to provide students with broad knowledge and skills regarding BIM and other digital technologies for construction management aspects focused on documentation, communication, constructability review and analysis in construction projects.
learning_outcomes: Explain the principles and functions of a Common Data Environment (CDE) within Building Information Modelling (BIM).
Establish and use Common Data Environment (CDE) for communication and collaboration in construction projects.
Use International BIM standards to produce necessary BIM documentation and manage information requirements at various stages of a construction project
Apply BIM coordination processes to integrate multidisciplinary models and facilitate effective communication among project stakeholders
Review and analyse constructability issues using BIM and other digital technologies, including augmented/ virtual/ mixed reality (AR/VR/MR)

title: Virtual Production Workflows
syllabus_overview: This unit introduces students to the creative technologies used for virtual production. Students will learn the basic workflow of virtual production through hands-on experience with a range of screen technologies that combine VFX, game engines, and live-action production delivered in Swinburne's Virtual Universe, an specialist built LED volume. Upon completion students will have further developed an understanding of the visual storytelling workflow offered through the integration of these creative screen technologies.
learning_outcomes: Develop a unified and coherent approach to Virtual Production workflows reflecting innovative and industry aligned creative practices.
Apply and integrate a range of creative technologies that deliver live in-camera visual effects using game engines, VFX, and live action production techniques in a LED-volume.
Apply collaborative teamwork skills within a virtual production environment.
Safely deliver studio production techniques using real-time game engines integrated with basic camera and lighting techniques for visual storytelling.
Reflect on visual storytelling techniques and indigenous knowledges for Film, Television and Screen, Games and Animation within virtual production environments.

title: Cyber Security: the people and organisation
syllabus_overview: This unit provides an advanced understanding of managing cyber security and its significance in enabling organisations to operate effectively within a fast paced, increasingly complex and diverse global environment. The management role will be examined from the perspective of direction-setting, decision-making and strategic planning; the organising role covering structure and design, communications and information technology, human resource management and the management of change and innovation; the leadership role covering the basics of organisational behaviour, group and team dynamics, motivation and leadership styles; and the controlling or performance management function introducing operations and value chain management within a specialised workforce.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate coherent and advanced knowledge of managerial functions of planning, organising, leading and controlling across the organisation in diverse and complex environments
Critically analyse the relevance of Human Capital Management (HCM) in the strategic management of specialised cyber security staff
Critically analyse the strategic priorities associated with managing security in a complex business environment
Work collaboratively as a member or leader of a team and/or with stakeholders and implement methods for optimising collaboration

title: Road Construction
syllabus_overview: This elective unit will provide students with an extended knowledge in the specific discipline of road and pavement engineering. Topics include (i) survey techniques for road construction, (ii) construction project control, (iii) methods of subgrade stabilisation and use of geosynthetics, (iv) drainage requirements for pavement structures, (v) identifying and collaborating with stakeholders during construction projects, (vi) overall site and project management, and (vii) professional practice in road and street construction.
learning_outcomes: Differentiate between the planning, design, and construction processes for roads and streets and apply contemporary control measures through the planning, design, site investigation, and construction phases of a project and communicate those outcomes through professional reports (A2, A4, K3, K5, S3, S4)

Identify the applications of Real Time Kinematic (RTK)- Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) Techniques, Total Stations, and Digital Levels in road and street design and construction (K1, K2, K3, S3)

Identify construction methodologies for earthworks, subgrade formation, evaluating critical material characteristics (including modification options), and the integration of plant and equipment selection for placement in the road structure (K2, K3, K6, S3, S4)
Assess and evaluate the impact that water may have within the transport corridor and recommend appropriate options to control and manage water movement to protect the pavement (K1, K3, K6)
Develop a comprehensive approach to the management of construction sites to ensure their safety, good traffic management and the required access for local communities and businesses (A2, A4, K5, S4)
Assess, evaluate, and recommend road signage, furniture, and environmental landscaping within adjacent road reserves (K3, K5, K6, S1, S4)
Apply the principles of sound stakeholder engagement in road and street construction projects (K5, K6)

title: Advanced Undergraduate Bureau Internship
syllabus_overview: This unit is designed to extend and deepen undergraduate students’ understanding of professional design practice while cultivating advanced employability and leadership skills. Through an internship hosted by Swinburne University, students will engage in directed, experiential learning within a work-integrated context. They will apply design knowledge and methods to real-world projects for diverse clients, evaluate outcomes and develop leadership capabilities. Complementary learning activities will further enhance professional attributes, encouraging students to critically reflect on their industry experience and confidently articulate their emerging professional identity.
learning_outcomes: Proactively apply design practice knowledge and methods to tasks within a work integrated learning context
Effectively and collaboratively contribute to a professional design practice environment, including through leadership or mentoring
Lead preparation of design solutions in response to industry briefs that are informed by considerations of intellectual property, ethical practice and emerging technologies
Critically reflect on one’s design practice, plan strategies for personal development, and demonstrate development of professional purpose

title: Finite Element Methods and Applications
syllabus_overview: This unit provides the fundamental knowledge of application of numerical methods in civil engineering applications. Special focus will be on matrix analysis of structure and application of finite element methods to civil engineering structures.
learning_outcomes: Analyse a simple frame structure using the coordinate transformation method, i.e., to establish structural stiffness matrix for frame structures, to convert member loads to nodal loads, and to determine forces and moments in each member (K1, K3, S1, S2)
Describe the theory of finite element methods and the solution algorithms in the FE programs (K1, S1)
Select appropriate elements and formulate the structure accordingly to reproduce the real behaviour (K3, K4, S2)
Use a general purpose FE program to perform stress analysis for a simple structure and consider various behaviour of beams, plates, shells and continuum elements (K2, K3, K4, S1, S2)
Examine the stability of structures and determine the elastic buckling load (K1, K3, S1, S3)
Idealise and apply various loads to structures and determine the performance (K1, S3)

title: Cybersecurity Operations Management
syllabus_overview: Cyber security of an organisation concerns all stakeholders, employees and customers. This unit focuses on the management of resources and aims to develop and refine skills in stakeholder management and communications. Students will use a variety of methods to research communication protocols, cyber security principles, recovery and mitigation strategies.Students will use the frameworks that relate to information sharing and develop strategies for whole of organisation cyber security management. Some of the topics include communication protocols and strategies, security audits, security program development, incident handling, maturity models data governance, third party and supply chain risk.
learning_outcomes: Explain cyber security imperatives and implications to principle decision makers in an organisation
Critically evaluate the cyber security culture of an organisation
Analyse cyber security framework for an organisation against industry best practice
Examine the cyber security implications of the internet in relation to an organisation and the implications to business continuity
Examine and refine business continuity and disaster recovery plans and strategies as they relate to cyber security

title: Integrated Water Design
syllabus_overview: This unit provides the fundamental knowledge of the objectives, design and management strategies adopted for integrated water design. The unit will focus on the management of issues and design strategies related to both water quality and quantity within urban catchments and natural catchments supplying water to urban areas. Design of water infrastructure, including, weirs, storage dams and urban stormwater drainage will be explored. Students will be given the opportunity to develop skills in the application of computer models in the design and assessment of urban water management strategies, and use these models to develop a better understanding of the application of best design and management practice in integrated urban water systems.
learning_outcomes: Identify the fundamental objectives of urban water systems, including management of both water quantity and quality (K1, K2, K3, S1, S2, S3)
Identify the issues affecting the supply of potable water to urban communities (K1, K2, K5, K6, S1)
Analyse the processes by which floods are generated in urban drainage systems and the different mitigation strategies adopted (K4, K5, K6, A4, A5)

Interpret the processes by which pollutants are generated within urban catchments and the different processes used in the treatment of urban stormwater quality and develop treatment strategies for the management of urban stormwater quality (K5, A3, A6, S4)
Address the impact of urban stormwater on the ecosystems in urban stream systems (S2, S3, S4)
Formulate the use of life cycle costing to assess the suitability of different water management strategies (A1, A2, A3, A6)
Use computer based models to develop and investigate integrated urban water management strategies (K2, S4, A1, A4, A5, A6)

title: Advanced Software and System Security
