This unit provides students with an opportunity to apply concepts and principles of their discipline in an industry workplace setting and to better appreciate the nature of employment in industry. Academic frameworks will focus on studentâ€™s employability skills via participation, observation and reflection to gain invaluable insight into their discipline area of study and future world of work.
learning_outcomes: Negotiate realistic work objectives
Reflect on university learnings and disciplinary knowledge and compare them to the experience of industry practice
Demonstrate effective communication skills for a range of audiences, including industry
Evidence new learnings and employability skills from the workplace experience

title: Computer Modelling, Analysis and Visualisation
syllabus_overview: This unit aims to provide an appreciation of the various CAD/CAM/CAE tools available to the manufacturing industry, and practical experience in their use.
learning_outcomes: Identify the various CAD/CAM/CAE tools and their applications in the manufacturing industry (A3)
Apply computer modelling and analysis software tools in the design process (K1, K2, K3, K5, S1, S2, A1, A2, A4, A5, A6, A7)
Create and analyse surface models to assist the design process (K2, K3)
Create and analyse simple kinematic mechanisms (K1, K2, K3)
Evaluate CAD/CAE simulation results against experimental results (K1, K2, S2, A2, A4, A6, A7)
Describe the advances in modelling and the techniques available to industry, including virtual reality (K4, A2, A3, A4)

title: Accounting, Organisations and Society
syllabus_overview: This unit provides students with an understanding of contemporary developments in both financial and non-financial accounting, reporting and assurance. Students will gain insight into the research background and theoretical underpinning of contemporary developments as well as future research needs to support further development of accounting, reporting and assurance. In doing so the unit critically examines practice and policy developments in accounting, reporting and non-financial assurance to support the changing needs of investors and other stakeholders. The course material is addressed primarily through examination of academic research and contemporary professional pronouncements to facilitate examination of research approaches and theorising.
learning_outcomes: Critically evaluate the objective and development of non-financial corporate accounting, reporting and assurance
Critically evaluate the development and contemporary use of financial reporting on climate change and sustainable development issues
Critically analyse developments in contemporary accounting issues, research papers that address them and the research methods employed therein
Conduct research on contemporary accounting or reporting phenomena to solve accounting and reporting problems
Work individually or collaboratively to interpret and communicate accounting research

title: Biochemistry of Genes and Proteins
syllabus_overview: The unit aims to provide the students with fundamentals of the structures and functions of genes and proteins, an overview of the complexity, organisation and instability of the eukaryotic genomes, the structure, functions and mechanisms of regulation of eukaryotic genes, the genetic basis of various human diseases, the biochemical properties and functions of select proteins, an understanding of the applications of gene and protein analyses in diverse fields of modern biological and molecular sciences, and laboratory exercises that provide a greater understanding of these areas.
learning_outcomes: Recognise and summarise the structures and functions of examples of diverse types of genes, RNAs and proteins.
Discern the complexity of eukaryotic genes and genomes and their significance to cellular functions and evolution
Recognise and evaluate the many events and levels of regulation of gene expression, and their significance and applications in diverse areas including health, agriculture and emerging technologies.
Identify and describe the nature and major mechanisms of genetic variability, recombinations and/or instability in the human and other genomes, and the significance of these
Apply the principles of diverse molecular technologies to analyse genes or proteins for problem-solving and various applications

Apply laboratory skills and computer-based analysis to the above areas, including recording scientific observations correctly, analysing and interpreting these critically, and reporting professionally

title: Commercial Pilot Licence Additional Practicum
syllabus_overview: To facilitate further training to consolidate the procedural aspects of IFR cross country flight and / or to further consolidate proficiency in departure, en-route and arrival procedures in the conduct of commercial operations under VFR and IFR.
learning_outcomes: Be able to plan a flight considering all commercial legal operational requirements, based on accurate meteorological analysis, including en-route and take off and landing performance
Be able to prepare the aircraft including determining complete aircraft serviceability, fuel requirements and loading procedures including carriage of dangerous goods
Be able to manage passengers during normal and emergency operations
Be able to safely conduct IFR and VFR cross country flights according to GFS standard operating procedures for normal and non-normal in-flight scenarios complying with all airspace requirements
Be able to demonstrate proficiency in the application of instrument flight, on full and partial panel
Attain a Civil Aviation Safety Authority (CASA) Commercial Pilot Licence (Aeroplane)
Attain a Civil Aviation Safety Authority (CASA) Single-Engine Command Instrument Rating

title: Analysis for Competitive Advantage
syllabus_overview: This unit is designed to equip students with enhanced knowledge and in-depth understanding of management accounting concepts and technique application to achieve sustainable competitive edge. It addresses the interplay between competitive advantage and strategic management accounting in the context of contemporary operational environment. The link between strategy and resource management is emphasised, with the focus on value creation in achieving and maintaining a sustainable organisation.
learning_outcomes: Explain and demonstrate the role of management accounting in supporting strategy development and implementation
Identify and evaluate the strategic positions and strategic options of contemporary organisations to achieving sustainable competitive advantage
Apply appropriate strategic management accounting techniques to a range of complex business situations to improve value-creating activities in the day-to-day operations of an organisation
Apply divergent thinking, problem solving and research skills to solve cases in strategic management accounting and to communicate ideas both verbally and in writing
Work collaboratively in groups to conduct research on real-world scenarios while applying suitable analytical techniques

title: Private Pilot Theory for Managers
syllabus_overview: To introduce the student to flight planning, air law & procedures, navigation theory, meteorology, aircraft general knowledge, aerodynamics and human performance and limitations, at the Private Pilot level so that they may apply that knowledge to the management of aviation operations.
learning_outcomes: Explain the environmental, legal, engineering, and human factors that impact on flying operations at the Private Pilot level
Demonstrate an understanding of the principals involved in the safe and accurate, planning operations at the Private Pilot level
Apply the principles of flight planning and performance in managerial or operational roles to maximise operational benefit to an airline

title: Accounting Information and Managerial Decision Making
syllabus_overview: This unit provides students with the capacity to manage the finances of an organisation as well as to communicate financial decisions. Students are provided with the capacity to use financial information systems to inform decisions across a business
learning_outcomes: Apply critical and advanced knowledge and judgements and to take effective, ethical and timely actions regarding the current and future allocation of resources in the context of a complex global business environment
Apply advanced knowledge of quantitative skills, evaluate the assumptions, behavioural implications and qualitative factors in decision-making.
Critically analyse key problems, list uncertainties and develop strategies from accounting and financial statements
Apply decision making processes including interpreting bias, evaluating alternatives, organising information and clearly stating assumptions
Work in groups or individually solve problems using accounting information

title: Commercial Pilot Licence Theory 2
syllabus_overview: To provide students with the required aviation theoretical knowledge in the areas of Navigation, Operations, Performance & Planning, Flight Rules & Air Law for the Commercial Pilot Licence (Aeroplane), as well as flight under the Instrument Flight Rules (IFR), as detailed in the Civil Aviation Safety Authority (CASA) Part 61 Manual of Standards (MOS).
learning_outcomes: Explain the environmental, legal and human factors that affect flying operations at the Commercial Pilot Level under the Visual Flight Rules (VFR) and Instrument Flight Rules (IFR
Safely and accurately apply theoretical knowledge to flying operations at the Commercial Pilot Level under the VFR and IFR

Demonstrate an understanding of the unit content sufficient to pass the CASA Commercial Pilot Licence (Aeroplane) Theory Examinations for Navigation, Operations, Performance & Planning and Flight Rules & Air Law
Demonstrate an understanding of the unit content sufficient to pass the CASA Instrument Rating (IREX) Examination

assessment_tasks.task_name: CASA CPL Flight Rules & Air Law (CLWA) Examination (Individual)
CASA CPL Operations, Performance & Planning (CFPA) Examination (Individual)

title: Air Transport Pilot Licence Theory 2
syllabus_overview: To provide students with the required aviation theoretical knowledge in the areas of Flight Planning and Performance & Loading for the Air Transport Pilot Licence (Aeroplane) as detailed in the Civil Aviation Safety Authority (CASA) Part 61 Manual of Standards (MOS).
learning_outcomes: Explain the flight planning and performance considerations that affect flying operations at the Air Transport Pilot Level
Safely and accurately plan a flight, including performance & loading calculations, for the Boeing 727 according to CASA flight planning requirements
Apply an understanding of the unit content sufficient to pass the CASA Air Transport Pilot Licence (Aeroplane) Theory Examinations for Flight Planning and Performance & Loading

assessment_tasks.task_name: CASA ATPL Performance and Loading (APLA) Examination (Individual)

title: Private Pilot Licence Theory
syllabus_overview: To provide students with the required aviation theoretical knowledge for the Private Pilot Licence (Aeroplane) as detailed in the Civil Aviation Safety Authority (CASA) Part 61 Manual of Standards (MOS).
learning_outcomes: Explain the legal, engineering, aerodynamic, environmental and human factors that affect flying operations at the Private Pilot Level
Safely and accurately apply theoretical knowledge to flying operations at the Private Pilot Level
Demonstrate an understanding of the unit content sufficient to pass the CASA Private Pilot Licence (Aeroplane) Theory Examination

title: Flight Instructor Rating Additional Practicum
syllabus_overview: This unit provides additional supervised training for students who require further practice to complete the Flight Instructor Rating. Building on AVF80006, it revises and consolidates aeronautical knowledge, instructional skills and aircraft handling needed to plan, conduct and assess ground and flight training, using effective facilitation techniques grounded in competency-based training, briefing and debriefing, and Threat and Error Management. On successful completion, students meet the competency standards for the Civil Aviation Safety Authority (CASA) Flight Instructor Rating Grade 3 training and Night Training endorsements, qualifying them to deliver day and night flight training in line with CASA regulations and organisational procedures.
learning_outcomes: Apply specialised aeronautical knowledge from the CASA Part 61 Manual of Standards, and communicate the theoretical aspects of lesson topics clearly and accurately to students and assessors

Plan and conduct ground and airborne training using appropriate instructional and facilitation techniques, including questioning, teaching aids, lesson planning and management of the learning environment
Conduct clear, relevant and fluent pre-flight briefings and post-flight debriefings across the ground and airborne components of training
Operate the aircraft with sound judgement and precise technique across all manoeuvres to a standard exceeding that required for the Commercial Pilot Licence (Aeroplane) qualification

title: Auditing
syllabus_overview: This unit aims to familiarise students with the underlying concepts and objectives of auditing and the subsequent reporting function of the auditor. The unit covers theoretical and practical aspects of auditing, including auditing eCommerce systems, Continuous assurance and XBRL/SBR, the use of Data Analytics and Visualisations, as well as evolving considerations such as Blockchain and Cryptocurrencies.
learning_outcomes: Examine the nature and purpose of auditing within the regulatory auditing environment
Research, compose and report on critical and current topics in auditing
Work collaboratively in a team environment, to achieve set goals and illustrate knowledge of auditing
Explain the audit process and the need for financial report audits
Use the reporting framework of a financial report to assess possible outcomes

title: Accounting Systems and Reporting
syllabus_overview: This unit has four primary aims. The first is to build a sound understanding of both transaction recording and of the preparation of the main reports that are output from accounting information systems (AIS), along with the role of accounting professional ethics in these activities. The second aim is to build a sound understanding of management accounting foundations. The third is to build an understanding of AIS development processes/ methods and of accountants’ roles in the different stages of the systems development lifecycle. And the fourth is to unpack the implications and effects of digital disruption and digital business transformation on accounting functions, and on the required roles and competencies of accountants.
learning_outcomes: Apply accounting principles, concepts, and techniques to record business transactions, produce accounting reports, and support operational or strategic decision making

Understand and apply accounting information systems analysis, design, development, implementation, and maintenance processes and techniques, as well as the role of accountants in optimising these processes and techniques
Analyse financial as well as non - financial information to make meaningful comparisons between a business' past, present and future performance

Understand the effects of digital disruption and digital business transformation on the roles of accountants, and the range of different digital technologies accountants can leverage to supercharge accounting value creation

Apply and evaluate of the application of accounting professional ethics and business ethics in business decisions and practices, as well as of frameworks/standards (like IESBA and APES 110) that provide guidance on ethical values, norms, behaviours, and practices

title: Advanced Audit and Assurance
syllabus_overview: This unit provides a body of knowledge to understand the nature and diversity of audit and assurance engagements. The unit provides an insight on audit and assurance processes, the methodologies and procedures. It also examines the objectives of assurance engagements and current and future developments in assurance engagements. The environment within which the auditor or assurance practitioner operates, and the respective roles of the private and public-sector auditors and internal audit, are also discussed This unit integrates the materials from the CPA Program Professional Level segment titled Advanced Audit and Assurance and prepares students for the CPA examination. This is a core unit in the Master of Professional Accounting (CPA Specialisation) degree.
learning_outcomes: Critically evaluate the framework for assurance engagements in audit and review engagements and assurance engagements (other than audits or reviews)
Critically analyse the quality control standards for audit and assurance engagements, and the fundamental ethical principles for the auditing profession

Demonstrate coherent and advanced knowledge of the requirements of the audit, review and assurance standards that are applicable to audit and review engagements and assurance engagements (other than audits or reviews)
Apply the relevant auditing standards to the assessment for fraud and going concern in an audit of financial statements
Communicate proficiently and in professional practice and act as a leader or member of a team

title: Air Transport Pilot Licence Theory 3
syllabus_overview: To provide students with the required aviation theoretical knowledge in the areas of Flight Rules & Air Law, Meteorology and Navigation for the Air Transport Pilot Licence (Aeroplane) as detailed in the Civil Aviation Safety Authority (CASA) Part 61 Manual of Standards (MOS).
learning_outcomes: Explain the legal and environmental factors that affect flying operations at the Air Transport Pilot Level
Explain the purpose, operation and limitations of various navigation equipment and describe the navigation procedures commonly used at the Air Transport Pilot Level
Apply an understanding of the unit content sufficient to pass the CASA Air Transport Pilot Licence (Aeroplane) Theory Examinations for Flight Rules & Air Law, Meteorology and Navigation

assessment_tasks.task_name: CASA ATPL Flight Rules & Air Law (AALW) Examination (Individual)

title: Taxation
syllabus_overview: This unit provides students with valuable skills and knowledge to be able to apply taxation principles in a given scenario using legislative and judicial sources to make an informed decision.
learning_outcomes: Describe the key administrative components of the Australian taxation system and the basic principles of Australian income tax , fringe benefit tax and goods and services taxation legislation
Analyse, discuss and resolve issues relating to the determination of assessable income and allowable deductions
Explain taxation law that relates to the taxation of individuals and companies
Explain taxation law that relates to the taxation of partnerships, trusts and superannuation funds
Work collaboratively to analyse and communicate solutions to practical problems and case studies

title: Introduction to Biochemistry
syllabus_overview: The aim of this unit is to provide students with an introduction to the core concepts of relevance in the fields of biochemistry and biotechnology. This is done in two phases; the first is an introduction to the main classes of biomolecules within the cell, with a special emphasis on how the structure of these molecules determines their biological function, and the second is an examination of the major catabolic pathways, and how they are integrated into the overall metabolism of the cell.
learning_outcomes: Describe the properties of biomolecules and predict the behaviour of such molecules from their structure
Name and write structures for representative molecules of the major classes of biochemical
Interpret kinetic data and make predictions based on a simple model of enzyme kinetics
Design and interpret protocols for biochemical assays
Record, analyse and interpret data in the laboratory
Communicate the results of experimental work
Determine amounts and volumes in appropriate units from dilutions, unit conversions etc

title: Commercial Pilot Licence Theory 1
syllabus_overview: To provide students with the required aviation theoretical knowledge in the areas of Human Factors, Aerodynamics, Aircraft General Knowledge and Meteorology for the Commercial Pilot Licence (Aeroplane) as detailed in the Civil Aviation Safety Authority (CASA) Part 61 Manual of Standards (MOS).
learning_outcomes: Explain the engineering, aerodynamic, environmental and human factors that affect flying operations at the Commercial Pilot Level
Safely and accurately apply theoretical knowledge to flying operations at the Commercial Pilot Level

Demonstrate an understanding of the unit content sufficient to pass the CASA Commercial Pilot Licence (Aeroplane) Theory Examinations for Human Factors, Aerodynamics, Aircraft General Knowledge and Meteorology

assessment_tasks.task_name: CASA CPL Aircraft General Knowledge (CSYA) Examination (Individual)

title: Multi Crew Cooperation Additional Practicum
syllabus_overview: To provide additional supervised training that builds on AVF80005, giving students the further flight and simulator hours needed to consolidate and firmly establish competency in multi-crew flight deck operations. The unit reinforces technical proficiency, strengthens Crew Resource Management (CRM) skills for safe and efficient multi-crew operation, and embeds effective CRM and Threat and Error Management (TEM) practices across all phases of operations.
learning_outcomes: Operate the aircraft with precise instrument flying and effective automation management across all phases of flight
Apply air regulations, airline Standard Operating Procedures, and normal and abnormal checklists accurately and at the appropriate times in a dynamic multi-crew environment
Plan and conduct multi-crew flight operations through appropriate preparation, route knowledge and ATC compliance
Communicate intentions, briefings and requirements clearly and precisely with flight crew, cabin crew and passengers in a multi-crew environment
Apply Crew Resource Management (CRM) principles to function effectively as a team leader and crew member in both the Pilot Flying (PF) and Pilot Not Flying (PNF) / Pilot Monitoring (PM) roles

Evaluate dynamic, line-oriented situations and exercise high-level judgement and decision-making, applying CRM principles to integrate situational awareness, workload management and available resources
Analyse and mitigate threats and errors across all phases of operations by adopting appropriate Threat and Error Management practices

title: Multi Engine Aeroplane Instrument Endorsement Additional Practicum
syllabus_overview: To transition the student into the IFR environment at the higher level of competency required to manage a Multi Engine Aircraft.
learning_outcomes: Apply the appropriate flight planning principles to Multi Engine flight under the Instrument Flight Rules (IFR) considering all legal operational requirements
Use radio navigation aids and Global Positioning Systems for en-route navigation
Demonstrate proficiency in instrument flying, including well developed instrument scan technique and the ability to fly sector entries, holding patterns and instrument let down procedures
Demonstrate Multi Engine day and night circling approaches
Demonstrate sound Multi Engine aircraft and engine handling techniques
Explain the physiological effects and illusions associated with instrument flying
Conduct an IFR flight to the standard required to gain a Multi Engine Rating and Civil Aviation Safety Authority (CASA) Command Instrument Rating (Multi-Engine Aeroplane)

title: Air Transport Pilot Licence Theory 1
syllabus_overview: To provide students with the required aviation theoretical knowledge in the areas of Aerodynamics & Aircraft Systems and Human Factors for the Air Transport Pilot Licence (Aeroplane) as detailed in the Civil Aviation Safety Authority (CASA) Part 61 Manual of Standards (MOS).
learning_outcomes: Explain the aerodynamic, engineering and human factors that affects flying operations at the Air Transport Pilot Level
Describe the operational limitations of both aircraft and human beings at the Air Transport Pilot Level
Apply an understanding of the unit content sufficient to pass the CASA Air Transport Pilot Licence (Aeroplane) Theory Examinations for Aerodynamics & Aircraft Systems and Human Factors

assessment_tasks.task_name: CASA ATPL Aerodynamics & Aircraft Systems (AASA) Examination (Individual)

title: Aviation Research Methods and Statistics
syllabus_overview: This unit equips students to plan and design a major aviation research project. Students learn to formulate clear research questions and objectives, evaluate qualitative and quantitative research designs, search and synthesise relevant literature, and select appropriate methods for collecting and analysing data. An accessible introduction to statistical analysis supports students with minimal undergraduate statistics. Students also examine the ethical and risk-management considerations central to responsible research. Working with real aviation problems, they develop and clearly communicate a complete research plan in a professional report, building a strong foundation for advanced dissertation study.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse the principles of academic research and their application in aviation contexts
Evaluate the suitability, strengths and limitations of qualitative and quantitative research designs and methods for different aviation research questions
Analyse ethical issues in aviation research and recommend appropriate strategies for managing them
Formulate a research question or project objective and justify the selection of an appropriate, ethically managed research method
Design an appropriate structure for a major aviation research project
Synthesise and critically evaluate published aviation research in a formal literature review
Select and justify appropriate data analysis methods to support the design of a major aviation research project

title: Multi Crew Cooperation and Jet Orientation Course Practicum
syllabus_overview: To transition students from single-pilot to multi-crew operations by developing the Crew Resource Management (CRM) and Threat and Error Management (TEM) skills required for safe, efficient flight deck operation, while consolidating existing instrument flying and technical competence across all phases of flight, so that they operate with the autonomy, judgement and accountability expected of a multi-crew airline pilot.
learning_outcomes: Operate the aircraft with precise instrument flying and effective automation management across all phases of flight
Apply air regulations, airline Standard Operating Procedures, and normal and abnormal checklists accurately and at the appropriate times in a dynamic multi-crew environment
Plan and conduct multi-crew flight operations through appropriate preparation, route knowledge and ATC compliance
Communicate intentions, briefings and requirements clearly and precisely with flight crew, cabin crew and passengers in a multi-crew environment
Apply Crew Resource Management (CRM) principles to function effectively as a team leader and crew member in both the Pilot Flying (PF) and Pilot Not Flying (PNF) / Pilot Monitoring (PM) roles

Evaluate dynamic, line-oriented situations and exercise high-level judgement and decision-making, applying CRM principles to integrate situational awareness, workload management and available resources
Analyse and mitigate threats and errors across all phases of operations by adopting appropriate Threat and Error Management practices

title: Remote Pilot Licence Theory and Practicum (Multi-rotor drones up to 25kg)
syllabus_overview: The unit aims to deliver the Civil Aviation Safety Authority (CASA) Remote Pilot Licence (RePL) theory, the associated theory examination, practical flight training, and the flight test required for the issue of a CASA RePL. The licence covers small multi-rotor drones up to 25 kg gross weight, operated under visual line of sight (VLOS) and in accordance with CASA’s standard operating conditions (SOC). In addition, where required, students will also obtain an Aeronautical Radio Operator’s Certificate (AROC). This certification enables remote pilots to operate drones in controlled airspace, provided they also hold the necessary CASA approvals. An AROC allows remote pilots to broadcast over VHF radio aviation frequencies.
learning_outcomes: Apply regulations and policies during remotely piloted aircraft systems operations
Assess and manage operational safety risks during all normal and non-normal situations across all modes and stages of flight
Operate and manage all remotely piloted aircraft systems pre-flight, in-flight and post-flight
Operate aeronautical radios
Manage human factors in remotely piloted aircraft systems operations
Navigate remotely piloted aircraft systems

title: Aviation Research Dissertation - Human Factors
syllabus_overview: The aim of this unit is to enable students to apply the knowledge and skills gained during their Master of Aviation by coursework to an independent research project. Students will investigate a contemporary or emerging issue or challenge within aviation human factors and present their research findings in either an industry-appropriate report or an academic dissertation written in the style of a peer-reviewed journal article or conference paper.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate a contemporary or emerging issue or challenge in aviation human factors to establish its significance as a research topic
Construct and justify a research proposal that explains the topic, purpose, research questions, and rationale for an independent aviation human factors research project
Design, justify and describe an appropriate research methodology for investigating an aviation human factors research question
Analyse and interpret research findings effectively and appropriately in relation to the research questions, relevant literature, and aviation human factors context
Communicate an independent research project in an industry-appropriate report or academic dissertation that addresses the research questions and supports conclusions with evidence

title: Private Pilot Licence Theory
syllabus_overview: To provide students with the required aviation theoretical knowledge for the Private Pilot Licence (Aeroplane) as detailed in the Civil Aviation Safety Authority (CASA) Part 61 Manual of Standards (MOS).
learning_outcomes: Explain the legal, engineering, aerodynamic, environmental and human factors that affect flying operations at the Private Pilot Level
Safely and accurately apply theoretical knowledge to flying operations at the Private Pilot Level
Demonstrate an understanding of the unit content sufficient to pass the CASA Private Pilot Licence (Aeroplane) Theory Examination

title: Aviation Research Dissertation - Aviation Management
syllabus_overview: The aim of this unit is to enable students to apply the knowledge and skills gained during their Master of Aviation by coursework to an independent research project. Students will investigate a contemporary or emerging issue or challenge within aviation management and present their research findings in either an industry-appropriate report or an academic dissertation written in the style of a peer-reviewed journal article or conference paper.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate a contemporary or emerging issue or challenge in aviation management to establish its significance as a research topic
Construct and justify a research proposal that explains the topic, purpose, research questions, and rationale for an independent aviation management research project
Design, justify and describe an appropriate research methodology for investigating an aviation management research question
Analyse and interpret research findings effectively and appropriately in relation to the research questions, relevant literature, and aviation management context
Communicate an independent research project in an industry-appropriate report or academic dissertation that addresses the research questions and supports conclusions with evidence

title: Commercial Pilot Licence Theory 2
syllabus_overview: To provide students with the required aviation theoretical knowledge in the areas of Navigation, Operations, Performance & Planning, Flight Rules & Air Law for the Commercial Pilot Licence (Aeroplane), as well as flight under the Instrument Flight Rules (IFR), as detailed in the Civil Aviation Safety Authority (CASA) Part 61 Manual of Standards (MOS).
learning_outcomes: Explain the environmental, legal and human factors that affect flying operations at the Commercial Pilot Level under the Visual Flight Rules (VFR) and Instrument Flight Rules (IFR)
Safely and accurately apply theoretical knowledge to flying operations at the Commercial Pilot Level under the VFR and IFR

Apply the unit content sufficient to meet the knowledge requirements of the CASA Commercial Pilot Licence Navigation (CNAV) theory examination and the CASA Commercial Pilot Licence (Aeroplane) examinations for Operations, Performance & Flight Planning (CFPA) and Flight Rules & Air Law (CLWA)
Apply the unit content to meet the knowledge requirements of the CASA Instrument Rating Examination (IREX)

assessment_tasks.task_name: CASA CPL Flight Rules & Air Law (CLWA) Examination (Individual)
CASA CPL Operations, Performance & Planning (CFPA) Examination (Individual)

title: Private Pilot Licence Additional Practicum
syllabus_overview: This unit provides additional supervised flight training for students who require further flying hours beyond their initial Private Pilot Licence Practicum to meet the competency standards for the Civil Aviation Safety Authority (CASA) Private Pilot Licence (Aeroplane) flight test. Students further integrate Private Pilot Licence theory with practical flight experience while consolidating airmanship, aircraft handling, cross-country procedures, flight planning, communication and threat and error management skills under CAE OAA standard operating procedures.
learning_outcomes: Operate and manage the aircraft safely within its defined limitations and CAE OAA standard operating procedures
Exercise the responsibilities of pilot in command of a cross-country flight that may carry passengers, acting in a responsible and accountable manner

Plan and conduct a flight to a destination or alternate aerodrome under the applicable flight rules, including pre-flight preparation (aircraft serviceability, fuel requirements and loading), compliance with airspace and departure and arrival procedures, and navigation under normal and abnormal conditions
Manage aircraft systems, passengers and air traffic control requirements during normal and abnormal operations
Communicate effectively in English to at least ICAO Level 4 proficiency
Apply non-technical skills in threat and error management during flying operations
Integrate theoretical knowledge and practical flying skills to meet the competency standards required for a CASA Private Pilot Licence (Aeroplane)

title: Air Transport Licence Theory 1
syllabus_overview: To provide students with the required aviation theoretical knowledge in the areas of Aerodynamics & Aircraft Systems and Human Factors for the Air Transport Pilot Licence (Aeroplane) as detailed in the Civil Aviation Safety Authority (CASA) Part 61 Manual of Standards (MOS).
learning_outcomes: Explain the aerodynamic, engineering and human factors that affects flying operations at the Air Transport Pilot Level
Describe the operational limitations of both aircraft and human beings at the Air Transport Pilot Level
Demonstrate an understanding of the unit content sufficient to pass the CASA Air Transport Pilot Licence (Aeroplane) Theory Examinations for Aerodynamics & Aircraft Systems and Human Factors

assessment_tasks.task_name: CASA ATPL Aerodynamics & Aircraft Systems (AASA) Examination (Individual)

title: Flight Instructor Rating Practicum
syllabus_overview: This unit prepares students to plan, conduct and assess ground and flight training for professional flight crew licensing. Students apply and integrate advanced aeronautical knowledge, instructional skills and precise aircraft handling, using effective teaching and facilitation techniques grounded in competency-based training, sound briefing and debriefing, and Threat and Error Management. On successful completion, students meet the competency standards for the Civil Aviation Safety Authority (CASA) Flight Instructor Rating Grade 3 training endorsement and Night Training endorsement, qualifying them to deliver day and night flight training in line with CASA regulations and organisational procedures.
learning_outcomes: Apply specialised aeronautical knowledge from the CASA Part 61 Manual of Standards, and communicate the theoretical aspects of lesson topics clearly to students and assessors

Plan and conduct ground and airborne training using appropriate instructional and facilitation techniques, including questioning, teaching aids, lesson planning and management of the learning environment
Operate the aircraft with sound judgement and precise technique across all manoeuvres to a standard exceeding that required for the Commercial Pilot Licence (Aeroplane) qualification
Analyse and assess student responses during training, and apply corrective measures informed by the rates and stages of learning, automaticity and the foundations of expertise

Evaluate the cognitive basis of airmanship, including situational awareness, captaincy, prioritisation, load shedding and decision making, while managing threats and errors throughout instructional sequences

Design effective training curricula, syllabi and lesson plans, and apply appropriate assessment standards and techniques consistent with instructor professionalism and self-managed professional practice

title: Commercial Pilot Licence Theory 1
syllabus_overview: To provide students with the required aviation theoretical knowledge in the areas of Human Factors, Aerodynamics, Aircraft General Knowledge and Meteorology for the Commercial Pilot Licence (Aeroplane) as detailed in the Civil Aviation Safety Authority (CASA) Part 61 Manual of Standards (MOS).
learning_outcomes: Explain the engineering, aerodynamic, environmental and human factors that affect flying operations at the Commercial Pilot Level
Safely and accurately apply theoretical knowledge to flying operations at the Commercial Pilot Level

Demonstrate an understanding of the unit content sufficient to pass the CASA Commercial Pilot Licence (Aeroplane) Theory Examinations for Human Factors, Aerodynamics, Aircraft General Knowledge and Meteorology

assessment_tasks.task_name: CASA CPL Aircraft General Knowledge (CSYA) Examination (Individual)

title: Commercial Pilot Licence Practicum 2B
syllabus_overview: To consolidate the theory taught in AVT10002 and AVT20001 and integrate this theory into the practical flying training to obtain a Commercial Pilot Licence (A). To develop the skills and attributes of a professional pilot conducting passenger or cargo carrying operations.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate that they can safely operate a multi-engine aircraft within defined limitations to commercial and COAA standard operating procedures
Conduct aircraft pre-flight determining complete aircraft serviceability, fuel requirements and loading procedures and performance requirements in a multi-engine aircraft
Demonstrate that they can manage aircraft systems, passengers, company and air traffic control requirements during normal and abnormal operations
Demonstrate that they can conduct themselves in a responsible and accountable manner on cross country flights

Demonstrate the knowledge and skills to plan and conduct a commercial flight from departure aerodrome to a destination aerodrome, or alternative aerodrome, navigating the aircraft under the applicable flight rules. This includes pre-flight planning, compliance with airspace procedures and departure and arrival procedures, and navigation under normal and abnormal conditions
Demonstrate that they can conduct themselves in a responsible and accountable manner on VFR cross country flights as a professional pilot conducting passenger or cargo carrying operations
Apply the theory and practical knowledge gained to attain a Civil Aviation Safety Authority (CASA) Commercial Pilot Licence (Aeroplane) in a multi-engine aircraft
Demonstrate an ability to manage and maintain operational documentation and the need to maintain professional regulatory compliance and currency

title: Air Transport Licence Theory 2
syllabus_overview: To provide students with the required aviation theoretical knowledge in the areas of Flight Planning and Performance & Loading for the Air Transport Pilot Licence (Aeroplane) as detailed in the Civil Aviation Safety Authority (CASA) Part 61 Manual of Standards (MOS).
learning_outcomes: Explain the flight planning and performance considerations that affect flying operations at the Air Transport Pilot Level
Safely and accurately plan a flight, including performance & loading calculations, for the Boeing 727 according to CASA flight planning requirements
Demonstrate an understanding of the unit content sufficient to pass the CASA Air Transport Pilot Licence (Aeroplane) Theory Examinations for Flight Planning and Performance & Loading

assessment_tasks.task_name: CASA ATPL Performance and Loading (APLA) Examination (Individual)

title: Technology in Advanced Practice
syllabus_overview: This unit covers the use of technology for the assessment and management of the patient with musculoskeletal conditions/ injuries and strategies for the enhancement of performance in athletes
learning_outcomes: Critically review the potential role of technology in the examination and management of musculoskeletal conditions/ injuries
Adapt, and apply technology in the management of musculoskeletal conditions/ injuries and enhancement of performance
Apply evidence-based principles to the development of athlete screening and return to sport programs
Explain the role of an advanced practice physiotherapist within a multidisciplinary team in the management of musculoskeletal conditions/ injuries and enhancement of athletic performance
Develop evidence-based strategies for the prevention of injury

title: Multi Engine Aeroplane Instrument Endorsement Practicum
syllabus_overview: To issue the student with a multi-engine aircraft class rating to be used in the Commercial Pilot Licence test. To consolidate the theory taught in AVT20001 and integrate this theory into the practical flying training to obtain an Instrument Rating. To consolidate the procedural aspects of VFR cross country flight.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate that they can safely operate a multi-engine aircraft within defined limitations to commercial and COAA standard operating procedures
Conduct aircraft pre-flight determining complete aircraft serviceability, fuel requirements and loading procedures and performance requirements in a multi-engine aircraft
Demonstrate that they can manage aircraft systems, passengers, company and air traffic control requirements during normal and abnormal operations

Demonstrate the knowledge and skills to plan and conduct a multi-engine flight under the Instrument Flight Rules from departure aerodrome to a destination aerodrome, or alternative aerodrome. This includes pre-flight planning, compliance with airspace procedures and conducting instrument departure, en-route and arrival procedures using a variety of navigation aids, during normal and abnormal operations
Demonstrate that they can conduct themselves in a responsible and accountable manner on multi-engine IFR cross country flights
Apply the theory and practical knowledge gained to attain a Civil Aviation Safety Authority (CASA) Instrument Rating in a Multi Engine Aeroplane (MEA)
Demonstrate that they can conduct themselves in a responsible and accountable manner on IFR cross country flights as a professional pilot conducting passenger or cargo carrying operations
Demonstrate an ability to manage and maintain operational documentation and the need to maintain professional regulatory compliance and currency

title: Commercial Pilot Licence Practicum 1
syllabus_overview: This unit consolidates the procedural aspects of cross-country flight and introduces students to visual night flying, including night visual departure, en-route and approach procedures. Students are also introduced to basic instrument flying procedures, undertake aircraft upset prevention and recovery training, and accrue a significant portion of their command flight time. This unit is followed by a subsequent practicum through which students can complete the flight training required to obtain a Commercial Pilot Licence (Aeroplane).
learning_outcomes: Plan and execute day flights under the Visual Flight Rules (VFR), or night flights under the Night Visual Flight Rules (NVFR), in compliance with all legal operational requirements
Conduct safe night traffic pattern operations to CAE OAA solo standard in both normal and abnormal situations
Perform upset prevention and recovery manoeuvres in accordance with UPRT standards
Apply basic Instrument Flight Rules (IFR) en-route procedures, including sector entries and holding patterns
Exercise pilot-in-command responsibilities and accountability with increasing autonomy on cross-country flights, with or without passengers on board
Integrate the technical and procedural skills required to conduct a cross-country flight in Australian airspace

title: International Approaches to Crime, Punishment and Rehabilitation
syllabus_overview: This unit helps students understand Australia’s criminal justice systems by exploring how historical, social and cultural factors shape law, policy and criminal justice systems around the world. The unit explores how various jurisdictions conceptualise crime and the relative emphasis on rehabilitation and punishment in different countries. Furthermore, the unit explores how young people, women, people with mental health problems and those with intellectual disability who commit crime are treated following conviction and whether we can learn from other jurisdictions to improve Australia’s criminal justice systems.
learning_outcomes: Identify and compare how criminal behaviour is defined across different jurisdictions.
Analyse legal and social responses to crime in different jurisdictions.
Critically evaluate crime prevention and desistance strategies used internationally.

Apply comparative perspectives to assess local criminal justice practices and examine the influence of cultural, historical, political and resourcing factors to international rehabilitation approaches.
Examine the impacts of criminal justice policies on individuals and communities.
Formulate evidence-based arguments about how international approaches might inform local efforts to reduce crime and victimisation.

title: Private Pilot Licence Practicum
syllabus_overview: This unit enables students to consolidate the knowledge from Private Pilot Licence Theory (AVT10001 or AVT10005) and apply it through practical flying training. By integrating theory with hands-on flight experience, students build the airmanship, technical skills and judgement required to meet the competency standards for a Civil Aviation Safety Authority (CASA) Private Pilot Licence (Aeroplane).
learning_outcomes: Operate and manage the aircraft safely within its defined limitations and CAE OAA standard operating procedures.
Exercise the responsibilities of pilot in command of a cross-country flight that may carry passengers, acting in a responsible and accountable manner.

Plan and conduct a flight to a destination or alternate aerodrome under the applicable flight rules, including pre-flight preparation (aircraft serviceability, fuel requirements and loading), compliance with airspace and departure and arrival procedures, and navigation under normal and abnormal conditions.
Manage aircraft systems, passengers and air traffic control requirements during normal and abnormal operations.
Communicate effectively in English to at least ICAO Level 4 proficiency.
Apply non-technical skills in threat and error management during flying operations.
Integrate theoretical knowledge and practical flying skills to meet the competency standards required for a CASA Private Pilot Licence (Aeroplane).

title: Personality, Mental Health and Crime
syllabus_overview: This unit introduces students to the main types of personality and psychiatric disorders often linked to criminal behaviour. It helps students understand how different psychological factors can contribute to why people commit crimes or continue offending. The unit also explores how forensic mental health professionals assess, treat, and manage individuals who have both mental health issues and needs related to criminal behaviour.
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of forensic mental health professionals in providing services focused on individuals with dual mental health and criminogenic needs.
Discuss the key signs and symptoms of various personality and psychiatric disorders often linked to crime.
Illustrate how personality and psychiatric disorders have historically and currently factor into Australian legal decisions around mental fitness, mental impairment, and sentencing mitigation.
Critically evaluate public perceptions and research evidence linking personality and psychiatric disorders to crime.
Discuss how personality and psychiatric disorders are considered within the assessment and treatment of offending behaviour.

title: Air Transport Licence Theory 3
syllabus_overview: To provide students with the required aviation theoretical knowledge in the areas of Flight Rules & Air Law, Meteorology and Navigation for the Air Transport Pilot Licence (Aeroplane) as detailed in the Civil Aviation Safety Authority (CASA) Part 61 Manual of Standards (MOS).
learning_outcomes: Explain the legal and environmental factors that affect flying operations at the Air Transport Pilot Level
Explain the purpose, operation and limitations of various navigation equipment and describe the navigation procedures commonly used at the Air Transport Pilot Level
Demonstrate an understanding of the unit content sufficient to pass the CASA Air Transport Pilot Licence (Aeroplane) Theory Examinations for Flight Rules & Air Law, Meteorology and Navigation

assessment_tasks.task_name: CASA ATPL Flight Rules & Air Law (AALW) Examination (Individual)

title: Leading High Performance Organisations
syllabus_overview: This unit examines what it takes to lead high-performing aviation organisations in complex and safety-critical environments. Students explore how leaders balance commercial performance with reliability, safety, resilience, adaptability, and innovation across areas such as flight deck operations, air traffic control, maintenance, and airline operations. Drawing on organisational behaviour, leadership, human factors, resilience engineering, systems thinking, and high reliability organisations, students consider how effective leaders shape culture, teamwork, systems, and processes to support safe, reliable, and adaptive performance.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate high performance in the context of aviation industry organisations
Analyse competing priorities among efficiency, quality, reliability, safety, resilience, adaptability, and innovation as they apply in aviation contexts
Critique tensions between reliability and resilience, and between conformance and responsiveness

Critically compare the application of Normal Accident Theory (NAT), High Reliability Organisations (HRO), Resilience Engineering (RE), and Socio-Technical Systems (STS) as implemented across aviation contexts
Select and justify appropriate applications of NAT, HRO, RE, or STS across various aviation sectors and organisational areas
Synthesise principles that promote a high-performing organisational culture while balancing reliability, safety, resilience, adaptability, and innovation

title: Advanced Physiotherapy Practice 2
syllabus_overview: This unit covers advanced sports physiotherapy specific practice and the integration of evidence-based practice principles into clinical practice, within a sports and exercise physiotherapy context
learning_outcomes: Perform the assessment and management of the injured athlete using advanced sports physiotherapy skills
Construct and disseminate the findings of a research project
Produce the integration of research evidence, practice-based evidence, clinical expertise and patient preference into clinical sports physiotherapy practice.

title: Airline Revenue Management and Pricing
syllabus_overview: This unit introduces students to the commercial logic and practical tools used in airline revenue management and pricing. Students will examine how airlines forecast demand, segment customers, assign booking classes, manage seat inventory and spoilage, and use pricing strategies to support commercial performance. The unit also explores the links between revenue management, scheduling, marketing, distribution, sales, loyalty programs, and broader organisational strategy. Students will analyse airline deregulation, growth in air travel, the competitive impact of low-cost carriers, and contemporary approaches to performance monitoring, service marketing, and revenue management organisational models.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse the principles of passenger revenue management and their application to commercial aviation
Evaluate the key factors influencing seat demand
Appraise pricing as a strategic lever in airline demand management
Apply technical revenue management skills and strategies in airline contexts
Interpret and evaluate the different revenue management reports available to assess commercial performance
Critically evaluate the organisational structures and processes that support effective revenue management
Synthesise analysis, theory, and contemporary industry evidence on current airline revenue management practices and developments, using individual written communications

title: Clinical Reasoning
syllabus_overview: This unit covers the principles of advanced clinical reasoning and the integration with evidence-based practice in patient centred clinical practice
learning_outcomes: Apply principles of practice-based evidence across multiple models of clinical reasoning within a biopsychosocial framework to inform assessment and management in sports and exercise physiotherapy
Integrate client data, including imaging and pathology tests, in the clinical reasoning process in sports and exercise physiotherapy

Apply principles of person‑centred care that incorporate individual perspectives, including respectful communication, reflection, advocacy, safety, and quality, to support culturally safe and inclusive management in sports and exercise physiotherapy, including care for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples
Critically appraise the role of, and apply sports psychology principles in the assessment and management of clients in sports and exercise physiotherapy

title: Business Analytics in Healthcare
syllabus_overview: This unit will enable students to understand the role of data analytics in healthcare to improve patient outcomes, enhance operational efficiency.
learning_outcomes: Assess the roles, challenges, and value of data analytics in healthcare research, policy, and management.
Demonstrate critical thinking to identify, evaluate, and solve healthcare problems using data-driven, evidence-based approaches.
Design and implement strategies for collecting, managing, and utilizing healthcare data, including electronic health records.
Apply descriptive, predictive, and prescriptive analytics to improve patient outcomes, optimize resource allocation, and enhance operational efficiency.

title: External Placement A
syllabus_overview: This unit is the second placement unit, and students first external placement experience. Students will gain experience in the delivery of psychological services in real-world settings alongside the theoretical and simulated learning that takes place in the coursework units. The unit will provide opportunity for skill development in a supervised and structured environment where reflective practice is an important component of supervisory relationships. The aim is for students to further develop their clinical assessment, intervention, and case formulation skills consistent with a scientist-practitioner model. Professional ethics and behaviours, the development of confidence, and competence in the application of psychological practice skills is an integral component of this unit. This placement will be either in an education setting (eg school) or a general educational and developmental psychology setting
learning_outcomes: Integrate evidence-based psychological theory and practice to the relevant professional environment
Engage in ethical and professional psychological practice, consistent with current relevant legal frameworks, mental health practice standards and the occupational setting
Provide culturally safe, responsive, and high-quality psychological services that are responsive to the needs of clients and that consider broader socio-ecological systems

title: Educational and Developmental Psychologist Interventions
syllabus_overview: This unit prepares students to implement and evaluate evidence-based individual and group interventions to support pre-school, primary, secondary, and tertiary students with a range of psychological, learning, social-emotional, and mental health issues. Learning theories and Positive Behaviour Support strategies will be taught, and programs to support students with a range of learning disorders, disabilities, and school engagement needs will be a feature of this unit. Furthermore, students will gain skills in applying positive psychology approaches to individual, whole school, and system-wide interventions to improve multi-level wellbeing and behaviour and learn how to work effectively with multidisciplinary teams both within and outside the school context.
learning_outcomes: Implement individual and group interventions to support the psychological, learning, behavioural, and wellbeing needs of students in educational settings
Design evidence-based strategies to support the educational and developmental outcomes of students with a range of learning disorders, disabilities and school engagement needs
Apply positive psychology approaches to individual, whole school and system-wide interventions
Evaluate intervention effectiveness using single-case and multiple-case design methods
Develop cultural competency in delivering interventions that are responsive to the needs of students, schools, families, and communities, and that are considerate of their socio-ecological systems

title: Commercial Pilot Licence Practicum 2
syllabus_overview: This unit provides the practical flight training component of an integrated Commercial Pilot Licence program, with the underpinning theory delivered in Commercial Pilot Licence Theory 1 and 2 (AVT10006, AVT20003). Students will build technical proficiency in operating multi-engine aircraft and planning and conducting instrument flights. They will strengthen the aeronautical decision-making, situational awareness and professionalism required to conduct passenger and cargo operations safely, in accordance with Civil Aviation Safety Authority (CASA) requirements and industry best practice. On successful completion, students will meet the requirements to attain a Multi-Engine Aeroplane Class Rating, Multi-Engine Command Instrument Rating and Commercial Pilot Licence (Aeroplane).
learning_outcomes: Operate a multi-engine aircraft safely within defined limitations, in accordance with commercial and CAE OAA standard operating procedures
Conduct pre-flight preparation for a multi-engine aircraft, determining serviceability, fuel, loading and performance requirements

Manage and respond to aircraft systems, passengers, company and air traffic control requirements, evaluating requirements and executing the appropriate course of action during normal and abnormal operations

Plan and conduct a multi-engine flight to a destination or alternate aerodrome under the Instrument Flight Rules (IFR), including instrument departure, en-route and arrival procedures using a range of navigation aids under normal and abnormal operations

Plan and conduct a commercial flight, including passenger- and cargo-carrying operations, to a destination or alternate aerodrome under the applicable flight rules, including departure, arrival and navigation procedures under normal and abnormal operations
Integrate theoretical knowledge and practical flying skills to meet the competency standards required for a CASA Multi-Engine Command Instrument Rating and Commercial Pilot Licence (Aeroplane)
Exercise pilot-in-command responsibilities on cross-country IFR and VFR flights in a responsible and accountable manner, maintaining operational documentation, regulatory compliance and currency

title: Financial Information Systems
syllabus_overview: The aim of this unit is to introduce students to financial information systems, both manual and computer based. The basis of the unit is the accurate recording of all transactions following the principles of double entry accounting. In addition, students are introduced to the concepts of internal control and management accounting.
learning_outcomes: Explain the importance of accurate and timely recording of financial transactions following generally accepted accounting principles

Apply the rules of double entry accounting to manually and digitally record financial transactions in ledgers (general and subsidiary) and journals (general and special) and prepare financial statements.
Apply generally accepted accounting principles to the recording and interpretation of a range of business transactions.
Work collaboratively in a team environment to achieve set goals related to increasing knowledge of the accounting process.
Demonstrate an understanding of the implications of digital technologies and digital business transformation on the role of accountants and accounting practices.

title: Company Auditing
syllabus_overview: The broad objective of this unit of study is to familiarise students with the underlying concepts, objectives and reporting function of the auditor. The unit deals with both theoretical and practical aspects of auditing. The aim is to integrate the concepts of auditing with practical approaches taken by the auditor to ensure participants gain a complete picture of the audit process.
learning_outcomes: Apply coherent and advanced knowledge of the nature and purpose of auditing within the regulatory auditing environment
Utilise knowledge of research principles to plan and execute a piece of research on a critical and current topic of auditing
Operate effectively as a leader and member of a group to achieve set goals relating to building of knowledge of auditing
Critically evaluate the audit process and the need for financial report audits
Apply the concepts of good corporate governance and ethical business practice and their significance for the auditor
Demonstrate an understanding of financial audit in practice including the use of data analytics in the conduct of an efficient and effective audit.

title: Therapy Across the Lifespan
syllabus_overview: This unit provides students with opportunities to acquire evidence-based therapeutic skills, equipping them for the diverse field of educational and developmental psychological practice. These skills are designed to cater to clients spanning various age groups, cultural contexts, and settings, encompassing face-to-face and telehealth interactions, as well as individual and group modalities. Throughout the course, students will delve into evidence-based therapeutic interventions, trauma-informed and neurodiversity-affirming practices, and culturally safe ethical principles. Students will learn how to choose an approach to match the developmental, cultural, and individual needs of children, adolescents, adults, older adults, and families to promote wellbeing and engagement in the therapeutic process. There will be a focus on strengths-based positive psychology approaches to therapy in this unit. This approach aims to develop students' skills in promoting client resilience and preventing learning, behavioural, socio-emotional, and other mental health difficulties. Students will also examine the impact of historical and contemporary issues in psychological therapy, including for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities, and how these presently impact clients, communities, and the profession. Furthermore, this unit provides students with valuable hands-on experience through on-campus opportunities, allowing them to apply their skills in conducting effective psychological therapy across the lifespan.
learning_outcomes: Apply evidence-based knowledge of counselling and developmental theory to a range of presenting issues experienced by clients across the lifespan, including for diverse delivery modes and cultural contexts.
Implement ethical, culturally safe, trauma-informed, and neurodiversity-affirming therapeutic interventions with clients across the lifespan, using strengths-based approaches.

Competently and ethically apply and evaluate advanced therapeutic skills to prevent learning, behavioural, and social-emotional difficulties in a variety of educational and developmental psychology settings.

Critically analyse the impact of historical and contemporary issues in psychological therapy, including for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities, and how these presently impact clients, communities, and the profession

Engage in self-reflection and critical reflexivity on social positionality, values, beliefs, biases, and professional competencies to deliver culturally safe and anti-oppressive interventions that are responsive to the needs and socio-ecological contexts of clients.

title: Psychological Assessment in Educational Settings
syllabus_overview: This unit prepares students to select, administer, score, interpret, and report the outcomes of a selection of psycho-educational and mental health assessments that are most pertinent to the Educational and Developmental Psychologist’s role. Understanding culturally competent and ethical assessment practices in educational settings is embedded within this unit. Assessments that measure intelligence, academic achievement, behaviour, and common developmental and mental health disorders presenting in educational settings, as well as the importance of differential diagnosis, will be covered. Students will understand the theoretical and psychometric basis of such tests and will learn how to provide practical school and family specific recommendations for a range of client presentations, with a consideration of relevant socio-ecological systems.
learning_outcomes: Choose the most appropriate assessment for a range of common child, adolescent, and adult psychological, educational, behavioural, and mental health presentations in educational settings
Administer, score, interpret and communicate the results of a selection of psychological assessments that are most pertinent to educational settings.
Apply ethical and professional discipline specific practices to test administration, scoring, interpretation, and reporting in the context of culturally competent principles.
Demonstrate reflective skills and self-awareness of positionality regarding the use of assessment in educational settings

title: Professional Practice
syllabus_overview: This unit covers the aspects of a sports physiotherapists role that pertain to advanced professional practice.
learning_outcomes: Critically review and apply the principles of business, management and leadership within a sports physiotherapy context

Appraise the legal ramifications of practice within sports physiotherapy context including relevant professional and ethical codes, standards of practice, and legal and industrial requirements governing practice
Elaborate on the broader role of a sports physiotherapist within a multidisciplinary team including as an educator, communicator and advocate
Reflect on learning needs of an advanced practitioner and the potential role of the different professional development strategies

title: Natural Language Processing and GenAI
syllabus_overview: This unit introduces students to core Natural Language Processing (NLP) concepts and techniques with a strong emphasis on generative AI. It equips students with practical skills in text data preprocessing, feature extraction, and the design, training, and evaluation of text classifiers. The unit also covers methods for visualising and interpreting NLP outputs, and exposes students to an advanced NLP technique commonly used in contemporary generative AI systems.
learning_outcomes: Explain the concepts of computational linguistics in natural language processing
Analyse and transform textual data into suitable representations for text analytics.
Apply exploratory data analysis and visualisation techniques to textual data
Design, implement and evaluate text classification models for natural language processing tasks

title: Psychology of Criminal Behaviour
syllabus_overview: This unit guides students how to understand and examine psychological theories of crime and then apply guiding principles from these theories into effective correctional policies and practices. The unit will introduce the major empirical and theoretically informed psychological frameworks for understanding criminal behaviour, the major risk factors for criminal conduct, methodologies for assessing these risk factors, and importantly, the Risk Need Responsivity (RNR) model of correctional practice and how this model provides direction to policies in criminal justice agencies internationally.
learning_outcomes: Differentiate psychology-based risk factors for crime from biological and social explanations of criminal behaviour while situating these risk factors within general psychological models of human behaviour
Critically assess the role of research methodologies and empirical paradigms in the development of practice frameworks for correctional environments
Interpret incidents of criminal behaviour using an understanding of the major psychology-based risk factors for crime
Justify or question policies and practices in correctional environments using knowledge of empirically derived frameworks based in a psychological understanding of criminal behaviour

Construct recommendations about how correctional staff could address, manage, and reduce criminal behaviour using psychology-based practice frameworks, attending specifically to the unique characteristics of marginalised individuals (such as women, First Nations individuals, people with various diagnoses, etc.)
Evaluate the real-world challenges associated with effectively implementing psychology-based practice frameworks in correctional environments

title: Advanced Physiotherapy Practice 1
syllabus_overview: This unit covers advanced sports physiotherapy specific practices, including injury prevention, acute sports injury management and clinical management skills to optimise the athletes return to sport
learning_outcomes: Develop and adapt evidence-based strategies for injury prevention
Apply the principles of acute sports injury assessment and management
Manage injured athletes using advanced sports physiotherapy skill

title: Health Economics and Policy
syllabus_overview: This unit will focus on evaluating the cost-effectiveness of medical interventions, and understanding policies related to insurance, workforce, and health financing.
learning_outcomes: Apply economic reasoning to analyze health policy issues, such as health insurance, equity, and cost-effectiveness
Assess how economic evaluation informs public health decision-making and priority setting
Critique how government policy can influence health economic outcomes
Apply economic reasoning and quantitative evidence to support decision-making and policy evaluation

title: Economic Evaluation of Health Programs
syllabus_overview: This unit explores evidence-based, comparative analysis of costs and outcomes in different health programs. Other areas investigated include optimisation of resource allocation to ensure interventions are efficient and effective.
learning_outcomes: Interpret and critically assess economic evidence, including cost-effectiveness studies and health outcome measures
Critique the economic implications of health policy reforms and their impact on population health outcomes
Analyse and distinguish between the four main types of economic evaluations used in health programs.
Assess the economic impact of health and social policy interventions in an Australian context

title: Analysis of Economic Models and Data
syllabus_overview: This unit will provide students with an understanding for how mathematical representations and statistical methods are used to understand, simulate, and predict economic behavior and policy impacts
learning_outcomes: Apply economic and epidemiological data to model the costs and benefits of health interventions
Formulate and interpret economic models to address research or policy questions
Evaluate the assumptions, strengths, and limitations of economic models in healthcare
Analyse health economic and related datasets using appropriate statistical and econometric techniques.

title: Psychological Research and Evaluation A
syllabus_overview: Students will gain important professional skills in being able to critically evaluate and review contemporary scientific literature, with the aim of working collaboratively in a team to design a research project on a topic related to educational and developmental psychological practice. Research projects will be undertaken in small groups and align with one of the 17 United Nations Sustainable Development Goals. Students will also learn real-world skills in applying for ethical research approval, ensuring that their research and evaluation projects are underpinned by ethical research principles.
learning_outcomes: Critically evaluate contemporary scientific literature

Work with co-investigators to design a research study to investigate a topic relevant to the discipline of educational and developmental psychology and that aligns with one of the 17 United Nations Sustainable Development Goals
Initiate and lead research ethics approval through the standard Human Research Ethics Committee approval process
Understand how to engage in culturally competent research practices
Develop self-awareness and critically interrogate positionality, competency, and biases/prejudices in the context of research and evaluation practices

title: Assessment Across the Lifespan
syllabus_overview: This unit prepares students to conduct psychological assessments across the lifespan using evidence-based, culturally responsive, culturally safe, and ethically informed approaches. Students will develop competence in selecting, administering, scoring, interpreting, and evaluating psychological assessment methods, and in gathering and integrating information from multiple sources to formulate evidence-based understandings of client strengths, needs, and functioning. The unit emphasises the communication of assessment findings and recommendations, ethical and professional practice, risk management, and consideration of developmental, cultural, and contextual influences on assessment. Experiential learning activities provide opportunities to develop practical assessment skills relevant to contemporary psychological practice.
learning_outcomes: Conduct psychological assessments using evidence-based, culturally responsive, culturally safe, and ethically informed approaches, including the selection, administration, scoring, and interpretation of assessment methods across the lifespan.

Gather assessment information from multiple sources, including interviews, observations, psychometric measures, records, and collateral information, to understand an individual's functioning within their developmental and socio-ecological context.
Interpret and integrate assessment data to formulate evidence-based understandings of an individual's strengths, needs, functioning, and presenting concerns.

Communicate assessment findings, formulations, and recommendations safely, ethically, and effectively through professional oral, written, and/or digital communication tailored to clients and relevant others.
Evaluate the quality, utility, and outcomes of psychological assessments and recommendations to support evidence-based decision-making and ongoing monitoring of client needs.

Apply ethical, legal, professional, culturally responsive, culturally safe, and digital practice principles throughout the psychological assessment process, demonstrating professional reflexivity and adherence to professional standards.

title: Internal Placement
syllabus_overview: This unit facilitates the development of initial psychological practice skills required to work effectively and safely with clients, while also ensuring student progression is consistent with professional standards and professional competencies.
learning_outcomes: Integrate evidence-based psychological theory and practice in an appropriate professional environment
Engage in ethical and professional psychological practice, consistent with current relevant legal frameworks, mental health practice standards and the occupational setting
Provide culturally safe, responsive, and high-quality psychological services that are responsive to the needs of clients and that consider broader socio-ecological systems

title: Contemporary Issues in Educational Settings
syllabus_overview: This unit prepares students to use best-practice evidence to approach a range of contemporary issues relevant to the practice of educational and developmental psychologists. Topics will span across psychological practice with a diverse range of clients in rural, remote, and metropolitan areas, as well as pre-school, primary, secondary, and tertiary education settings. The unit prepares students to provide equitable support to all members within an educational community to promote whole educational-setting wellbeing and positive student learning outcomes. Supporting educational communities after a crisis and in an emergency, to implement the key principles of effective critical incident management, is an important skill learnt in this unit. This unit features on-campus opportunities for students to practice their skills in responding to contemporary issues in educational settings, and to hear from guest lecturers and experts working in the field.
learning_outcomes: Apply and evaluate evidence-based individual and group psychological interventions to support students, families and the broader educational community
Implement evidence-based critical incident management processes following a crisis or disaster.
Collaborate effectively with professionals from other disciplines to support educational communities.
Critique contemporary issues in educational settings related to individual and systemic issues and apply culturally competent and ethical practices to address these challenges
