title: Healthcare Operations and Project Management
syllabus_overview: This unit will provide students working knowledge for how operations and project management can optimize healthcare performance, by combining daily process efficiency with strategic, goal-oriented initiatives.
learning_outcomes: Critically evaluate how healthcare organisations are structured, including identifying and applying methods for operational improvement, efficiency and sustainability.
Formulate, plan and execute health-related projects, defining the scope, goals, and deliverables.
Evaluate and apply change management strategies, knowledge mobilisation, and evidence-based practices to drive improvement in healthcare.
Develop project plans based on research and best practices to address identified gaps in healthcare delivery, combined with evaluation plans to access outcomes and effectiveness.

title: Advanced Anatomy and Pathophysiology
syllabus_overview: This unit covers advanced knowledge on biomechanics, functional anatomy, and pathophysiology, that will underpin the examination, clinical reasoning and management of musculoskeletal injuries and conditions
learning_outcomes: Apply knowledge of biomechanical principles and functional anatomy/physiology to the assessment and management of common clinical conditions in the area of sports and exercise physiotherapy

Critically review, synthesise and apply advanced knowledge of pain sciences, physiology and pathophysiology in the assessment and management of common clinical conditions in the area of sports and exercise physiotherapy
Integrate advanced knowledge of functional anatomy, biomechanics and physiology to help optimise sports and exercise performance

title: Networks, Games, and Algorithms
syllabus_overview: This unit of study aims to provide students with mathematical knowledge and skills needed to support their concurrent and subsequent engineering, science and computer science studies. Students will gain experience in understanding and writing proofs and develop skills for creating and analysing algorithms, for a range of topics in combinatorics, graph theory, network theory, finite group theory, and mathematical games.
learning_outcomes: Write computer code to implement network, graph theoretic, and cryptographic algorithms, and to study mathematical puzzles and games.
Characterise algorithm performance using big O notation
Analyse real-world networks by applying network algorithms
Construct mathematical proofs for problems in discrete mathematics

title: Strength and Conditioning for Physiotherapists
syllabus_overview: This unit covers the prescription, delivery, adaptation, and evaluation of safe and effective evidence-based movement, physical activity, exercise, and strength and conditioning interventions to optimise health status, function, recovery, independence, and participation across the full health spectrum.
learning_outcomes: Apply advanced knowledge of exercise physiology, motor control and strength and conditioning principles to the assessment, management and prevention of sport and exercise related conditions
Design, implement and review conditioning, training programs to improve athletic performance

Select and use appropriate modes of communication to transmit evidence-based knowledge to specialist and non-specialist audiences to inform, motivate and effect change at the individual, and community level.

Apply advanced knowledge of exercise physiology, motor control and exercise prescription to analyse and develop exercise-based solutions for clients across diverse population groups, including age-related, cultural, gender-diverse and in various extreme environmental contexts such as thermal, stress and variable training conditions.
Critically review and apply best practice in health promotion with a focus on physical activity and exercise behaviours across all individuals and population groups

title: Infrastructure Project Management
syllabus_overview: This unit of study aims to introduce advanced concepts, managerial principles and techniques to plan and manage infrastructure projects effectively and efficiently.
learning_outcomes: Relate useful concepts, principles and management theories to infrastructure project activities and organisations
Identify stakeholder requirements and risks; and select infrastructure project management techniques and tool
Apply a systems engineering approach, including management of changes to scope, initiate and execute a successful project delivery

title: Applied Health Economics
syllabus_overview: This unit will explore economic theories, models, and statistical techniques to solve real-world healthcare challenges.
learning_outcomes: Develop and communicate economic arguments and analysis in written and oral forms
Design and implement a health economic analysis and solution for a healthcare provider
Interpret and communicate the results of model-based analyses to both technical and non-technical audiences
Implement either regression or simulation models to test economic hypotheses and forecast outcomes

title: Integrated Circuit Design
syllabus_overview: The aim of this unit is to equip students with the required engineering skills to design and implement integrated circuits, with an emphasis on front-end design. The objectives of this unit are to expose students to techniques and design methodologies in integrated circuit design. Students will develop skills in modelling, simulation, verification, testing, and implementation using industry-standard Electronic Design Automation (EDA) tools. Upon satisfactory completion of this unit, students should be able to carry out the design of an integrated circuit from requirement analysis through to implementation.
learning_outcomes: Design, troubleshoot, simulate, analyze and synthesize digital integrated circuits using hardware description language such as VHDL, Verilog, etc. (K2, K3, K4, S1, S2, S3)
Implement and test designed logical functions on a configurable integrated circuit. (K2, K3, K4, S1, S2, S3)
Apply the working principles of digital integrated circuits to interpret, analyze and address design-related problems. (K2, K3, K4, S1, S2, S3)

title: Managing Quality and Safety in Infrastructure Engineering Projects
syllabus_overview: This micro-unit aims at providing advanced exposure to the fundamentals and specialised aspects of quality management and safety in infrastructure construction projects.
learning_outcomes: Apply relevant quality management systems in infrastructure engineering projects
Recognise construction quality issues and create strategies on how to mitigate quality deviations and non-conformances
Implement and administer Workplace Health and Safety procedures responsibly and autonomously in construction site operations

title: Cultivating Creativity
syllabus_overview: This micro-unit, Cultivating Creativity will enable you to nurture and apply your creativity to add and unlock new sources of value to you and your organisation. The micro unit dispels some of the pervasive myths about creativity and examines the three major components of creativity that need to be used in business contexts. Working alongside Swinburneâ€™s creativity experts, you will discover where your creativity is, what you need to do to enhance it in you and your organization to both unlock and add value. You will use proven methods to expand your creative repertoire, including creative exercise, activities and tactics. This unit will enable you to hone the skills and tools needed to build the creative foundations in you, your organization and workplace.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate your personal creativity using evidence-based methods
Critically analyse barriers to creativity and apply different tools to respond to them
Critically analyse creativity tools for you, your team and organisation

title: Integrated Care
syllabus_overview: This unit covers the development and implementation of comprehensive assessment and management strategies for complex conditions in musculoskeletal and sports physiotherapy.
learning_outcomes: Critically review, adapt and implement advanced knowledge, skills and clinical reasoning in the examination and management of musculoskeletal conditions/ injuries related to sports and exercise physiotherapy across a range of sports

Critically appraise the role of common pharmacological interventions used in the management of musculoskeletal conditions and injuries, including indications for prescription, mechanisms of action, and potential adverse effects.
Explain the role of food and nutrition in the prevention and management of musculoskeletal conditions/ injuries
Apply advanced neuromusculoskeletal assessment skills in the examination of musculoskeletal conditions and injuries related to sports and exercise physiotherapy

title: Ethical Psychological Practice and Leadership
syllabus_overview: This unit teaches students to critically synthesise and apply culturally safe, ethical, legal, and professional principles across the lifespan in a range of educational and developmental psychological practice settings. A particular focus is ethical practice and leadership within educational settings. Students learn evidence-based strategies to lead systemic change in educational policy and processes, taking a health equity and human rights approach to prevent learning, behavioural, social-emotional, and other mental health difficulties and achieve equitable outcomes for individuals, groups, and communities. They also build skills in ethical and professional consultation and capacity-building with stakeholders to strengthen student, school, family, and community resilience and wellbeing, including understanding the roles of other service providers. Students will develop their capacity for self-reflection and critical reflexivity on their own social positionality, values, beliefs, biases, and professional competence, recognising when to seek supervision, professional development, and referral.
learning_outcomes: Critically synthesise and apply culturally safe, ethical, legal and professional principles in a range of educational and developmental psychological practice settings to support individuals and groups across the lifespan.
Employ advanced leadership skills, using a health equity and human rights approach, to promote systemic changes to educational policy and processes.
Advocate for equitable outcomes for individuals, groups, and communities affected by learning, behavioural, social-emotional, and other mental health difficulties.

Utilise consultation and capacity-building skills to support a range of education stakeholders to improve student learning, resilience, and wellbeing, including making appropriate referrals, recommending reasonable adjustments, and understanding the roles of other service providers.

Engage in self-reflection and critical reflexivity on social positionality, values, beliefs, biases, and professional competencies to recognise when to seek supervision, professional development, or referral.

title: Innovation Strategy as a tool of Entrepreneurship
syllabus_overview: This micro unit examines key theories of innovation within the context of the innovation life cycle to understand how effective innovation strategy can be used as a tool in entrepreneurship. New ventures, businesses, organisations and corporations use innovation strategy to drive growth through value. Understanding the elements of innovation strategy, and its role within the organisation's system, is imperative for sustainable innovation. Students will also explore tools and techniques that will facilitate your understanding of the barriers and enablers of innovation within the organisation.
learning_outcomes: Apply coherent and advanced knowledge of new venture creation and innovation practice in the corporate lifecycle
Critically evaluate the role of co-creation and collaboration in the innovation life cycle.

title: Creating Exceptional Experiences: Designing Products and Services that Meet People’s Needs
syllabus_overview: This micro-unit takes the view that great products and services are designed with people in mind. Creating Exceptional Experiences will introduce the tools you need to walk in your customerâ€™s shoes, and see the world from their perspective. Using proven tools and methods to uncover your customerâ€™s needs, including design thinking, youâ€™ll learn how to identify and reframe problems, and make better decisions by putting your customer first. You will apply creative thinking and innovation techniques to test and interrogate your assumptions and explore how human-centred design can help you develop solutions that inspire and delight. By the end of this micro unit, you will know how to develop a complete picture of your customer, identify their concerns and desires, and have a detailed process to develop products and services to address peopleâ€™s real needs.
learning_outcomes: Apply advanced knowledge of the key principles of evidence-based product and service design
Critically analyse the foundation elements of a transferable customer-focused design and innovation process
Apply advanced knowledge of human-centred design principles to tackle complex challenges

title: Ethics and Law for Health Businesses
syllabus_overview: This unit will integrate clinical bioethics with commercial regulations to inform students of key areas of patient safety, legal compliance, and ethical high-quality care.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate the relationship between law and ethics in healthcare, considering the impact of legal, moral, political, and social factors.
Examine and apply common law, statutory requirements, and regulatory frameworks to health service management and clinical practice.
Apply ethical theories to complex dilemmas, such as end-of-life care, resource allocation, and patient rights.
Justify and defend informed positions on contentious health issues in a respectful and persuasive manner.
Evaluate governance structures, policies, and risk management strategies within healthcare organizations to ensure quality and safety.

title: The Entrepreneur’s Toolkit: A Masterclass in Getting from Idea to Start Up
syllabus_overview: This micro-unit investigates that bringing a great business idea is more than just luck. There are well-honed tools that can help you to craft a good concept into a great business. The Entrepreneur's Toolkit is a hands-on guide to taking your business idea from concept to reality. You will work with Swinburne's experts on entrepreneurship and innovation to craft a business idea into an actionable plan using a range tools including business model canvas, lean startup methodology and communicating your ideas to peers and mentors for feedback and further refinement. The Entrepreneur's Toolkit is suitable to both entrepreneurs and intrapreneurs, whether you're working on a commercial start up or a social enterprise.
learning_outcomes: Apply coherent and advanced knowledge of concepts, techniques and tools of entrepreneurship and innovation
Communicate and sell innovative new business ideas successfully
Apply the fundamentals of entrepreneurship and plan to operationalise a business model

title: Health Service Administration and Management
syllabus_overview: This unit will provide students knowledge and experience in how to manage teams, budgets, and technology in various health settings, such as hospitals or clinics.
learning_outcomes: Appraise and apply management, leadership, and organizational theories to navigate complex health service environments
Apply principles of financial information and resource allocation to healthcare organisations, to understand strategic leadership and resource management.
Analyse the basic elements of health system policy and compare domestic and international reforms to contextualise policy initiatives and reforms.
Evaluate patient care safety and apply tools for quality measurement, assurance, and continuous improvement.
Examine epidemiological and statistical principles to research complex problems and evaluate health program outcomes to form evidence-based decision making.

title: Introduction into Health Economics
syllabus_overview: This unit introduces students to the role of health economics in maximizing health outcomes by efficiently allocating limited resources (time, money, technology) to competing interventions.
learning_outcomes: Explain key economic concepts and principles relevant to health and healthcare systems
Review and describe the role of economics in understanding healthcare resource allocation, financing, and efficiency
Assess how different economic models can be applied to healthcare
Compare different healthcare systems and models of funding, identifying their economic implications for access, quality, and sustainability

title: Shaping the Context for Innovative Organisations
syllabus_overview: This micro-unit focuses on what leaders can do to cultivate a work environment that fosters creativity and innovation. Students will learn a variety of problem solving, design and decision-making methodologies to support innovative solutions to complex problems.
learning_outcomes: Apply problem solving, design and decision-making methodologies to identify and provide innovative solutions to complex leadership and innovation problems with intellectual independence.
Apply advanced knowledge to evaluate appropriate frameworks and tools to embed creativity and innovation within an organisation.

title: Developing the Leaders for Innovative Organisations
syllabus_overview: This micro-unit focuses on the role and development of the leader, and the practice of leadership in the context of organisational creativity and innovation. Students will critically examine the concept and practice of leadership, focussing on theories and practices that enhance creativity and innovation in organisational settings.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse the relationship between leading innovative activities and the entrenched views in organisations, with clear articulation of the ideas underpinning your approaches.
Understand the connection between leadership practices and decision-making in designing a creative organisation and culture.

title: Procurement, Contracts and Construction Law Fundamentals
syllabus_overview: The aim of this micro-unit is to introduce the fundamental aspects of procurement, contracts and the law related to construction and infrastructure management projects.
learning_outcomes: Apply procurement principles and fundamentals of various procurement systems for infrastructure project delivery
Identify the fundamental laws and legal requirements applicable to construction contracts and contract administration in projects
Plan contractual and professional responsibilities and facilitate alternative dispute resolution mechanisms suitable for infrastructure project delivery

title: Fundamentals of Road and Rail Infrastructure Engineering
syllabus_overview: This micro-unit of study aims to introduce the fundamentals of road and rail infrastructure design and construction.
learning_outcomes: Describe and analyse the transport planning process, including design principles and performance measures
Distinguish and apply suitable construction methods for rail and road transport infrastructure
Identify and evaluate the fundamentals of the signalling system and operations

title: Sustaining Corporate Innovation
syllabus_overview: This micro unit examines how corporate leadership, ethical values and management strategies facilitate and sustain entrepreneurial and innovation business practice. The successful innovating organisation is characterised by a culture that supports innovation and corporate entrepreneurship. Understanding the impact of corporate leadership and ethical values on innovation culture will enable you to identify and implement those practices that will facilitate successful corporate entrepreneurship. Students will also explore tools and techniques that can be used to understand the culture and entrepreneurial orientation of a business.
learning_outcomes: Critically evaluate ethical behaviour in corporate innovation.
Critically evaluate the impact of innovation cultures on corporate entrepreneurship.

title: Entrepreneurial Mindset and Intuitive Decision Making
syllabus_overview: This micro unit examines the behavioural characteristics exhibited by successful entrepreneurs to understand how these contribute to effective entrepreneurial action. Entrepreneurship is a mindset, a specific way of seeing and thinking and acting in the world. Cultivating an entrepreneurial mindset will enable students to nurture and apply their own entrepreneurial characteristics to identify potential entrepreneurial opportunities. Students will also use tools and techniques to measure and develop their own entrepreneurial mindset.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse the behavioural characteristics of entrepreneurs.
Understand the connection between entrepreneurial mindset, intuitive decision making and opportunity recognition

title: Engaging the Followers for Creativity and Innovation
syllabus_overview: This micro-unit focuses on engaging followers in the context of organisational creativity and innovation. Students will examine the factors that underpin productive leader-follower relationships, focussing on the conditions that foster trust and a climate of psychological safety.
learning_outcomes: Reflect on and take responsibility for their own learning and self-management processes, and manage their own time and processes effectively by regularly reviewing performance as leaders of innovation in organisational settings.
Critically analyse the role of individuals in building an organisational environment that has creativity and innovation at its core.

title: Cost Planning and Management with 5D BIM
syllabus_overview: The aim of this micro-unit is to provide a specialised primer for project cost planning fundamentals and advance management with 5D BIM technologies.
learning_outcomes: Identify direct and indirect costs in engineering infrastructure projects and apply estimating principles for project cost estimates
Use and evaluate earned value metrics for monitoring and controlling project costs
Describe how 5D BIM supports the calculation of cost estimations

title: Resource Scheduling and 4D BIM
syllabus_overview: This micro-unit of study aims to introduce scheduling principles and advanced tools/ techniques for efficient resource scheduling in engineering infrastructure projects.
learning_outcomes: Students who successfully complete this micro-unit will be able to:Identify resource characteristics and constraints and implement successfully project scheduling requirements
Examine appropriate techniques and advanced tools for resource scheduling in engineering infrastructure projects
Identify the benefits of 4D BIM in planning and managing infrastructure projects

title: Business Analytics
syllabus_overview: This micro-unit focuses on business analytics and equipping students with the relevant data analytics skills required to solve the complex data problems of modern businesses. Students will have the opportunity to learn about evidence based decision-making, online analytical processing, big data and various tools and techniques to perform descriptive, predictive and prescriptive analytics and their application in various domains.
learning_outcomes: Critically evaluate the concepts of descriptive, predictive and prescriptive analytics and their application in various organisational contexts.
Select/recommend appropriate data analytics tools and techniques to implement a business analytics strategy.

title: Strategic Planning of Business Analytics Projects
syllabus_overview: This micro-unit examines the concepts, issues and challenges that are critical for implementing, maintaining and completing business analytics projects. Students will examine business analytics from a strategic perspective and examine how an organisation's industry, culture and structure influence the approach taken.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate coherent and advanced knowledge of organisational strategy and the principles of business analytics and align these to project management.
Critically evaluate project management and business analytics practices, methodologies, tools and techniques.

title: Data Visualisation
syllabus_overview: This micro-unit focuses on data visualisation and equipping students with the relevant visualisation skills to assist in visualising business-related datasets. Students will have the opportunity to learn about data visualisations and various tools and techniques to present data in various domains and formats.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse the concept of data visualisation and its application in various organisational contexts and datasets.
Critically evaluate and choose appropriate data analytics tools and techniques to implement data visualisation.

title: Data Analysis Fundamentals
syllabus_overview: The global economy has long entered the 'Age of Analytics' as the exponential growth in the volume of available data has converged with the development of more sophisticated algorithms, advances in computational power and the availability of cloud data storage. As a result, businesses that produce vast amounts of data must now harness that asset as a key source of their ongoing competitive advantage, which in turn is driving a dramatic increase in demand for analytical capability. This course will provide professionals with the skills required to begin a career in this huge growth area, or add analytical capabilities to their existing skill set in order to be more effective in a data driven world.
learning_outcomes: Apply statistical techniques to solve business problems
Visualise basic data in spreadsheets to inform a hypothesis
Create queries and aggregate results over multiple data sets using SQL
Evaluate and select appropriate data visualisation techniques
Create an interactive dashboard using Tableau to evaluate your hypothesis
Articulate best practice for working with data and highlight ethical considerations

title: FinTech Footprint: New Imperatives for Data Driven Business Models
syllabus_overview: This micro-unit focuses on the mainstream FinTech-led business models aiming at equipping students with the relevant business model innovation and disruption skills required to become aware, understand and adopt the relevant financial technologies applications within the different financial services sub-sectors. Students will have the opportunity to learn about the frameworks and theories of business models, and gain exposure to the characteristics, attributes and changes of key FinTech-driven business models essential for financial services organisations and startups to take advantage of the FinTech-related Australian and international opportunities available.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate coherent and advanced knowledge of emerging technologies for digital transformation towards the development of customer-centric architectural designs in financial services.
Critically evaluate frameworks and theories on business models and disruption to analyse emerging business models in financial services.

title: FinTech Handbook: Digital Regulation and Compliance Insights
syllabus_overview: This micro-unit focuses on the key FinTech-related regulatory frameworks and compliance requirements aiming at equipping students with the relevant skills required to become aware, monitor and navigate across the complex regulatory and compliance implications and developments due to the emergence of FinTech innovation. Students will have the opportunity to learn about the FinTech-related regulatory environment that is essential for organisations and startups to take advantage of the FinTech-related Australian and international opportunities available. Students will also put together a regulatory and compliance roadmap that is conducive to innovation and growth in various financial services and FinTech domains.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate coherent and advanced knowledge of the key FinTech-related regulatory frameworks and compliance principles and align these to financial technology applications.
Critically evaluate the areas where regulation and compliance are impacted by new and emerging financial technologies and align these to the strategic objectives of organisations.

title: FinTech Toolkit: Strategic Decision Making and Intelligent Practices
syllabus_overview: This micro-unit focuses on key strategies aiming at equipping students with the relevant strategic thinking and decision-making skills required to make strategic decisions on emerging financial technologies and disruptive FinTech ventures. Students will have the opportunity to learn about the key strategies and frameworks global financial services organisations utilise in order to differentiate themselves, along with, determining the role data-driven financial technologies can play in creating value for an organisation and helping an organisation stay ahead of FinTech disruption.
learning_outcomes: Critically evaluate the role of intelligent automation and data-led financial technologies in conjunction with the right organisational capabilities required for strategic decision making of FinTech evolutionary transformation.

Demonstrate the ability to develop a holistic FinTech innovation roadmap to reach strategic priorities, as well as catalyse, capitalise and monetise transformative innovation, sustainable growth and transient competitive advantage.
